descriptions.en: New Year's Day marks the beginning of a new calendar year and is one of the most universally celebrated occasions around the world. People gather with family and friends to welcome new beginnings, set resolutions, and share hope for the year ahead.

Cuba marks January 1 as both New Year's Day and the Day of the Revolution, celebrating the triumph of the Cuban Revolution in 1959 when Fidel Castro's forces entered Havana after the flight of dictator Fulgencio Batista.

World Braille Day celebrates the birthday of Louis Braille, the inventor of braille, and raises awareness of the importance of braille as a means of communication for blind and visually impaired people worldwide.

World Spaghetti Day on January 4 celebrates one of the most popular pasta dishes in the world. It is a day to enjoy a delicious plate of spaghetti with family and friends and appreciate Italian culinary tradition.

slogans.en: Twirl It. Slurp It. Love It.

descriptions.en: Epiphany commemorates the visit of the Magi to the infant Jesus. It is a public holiday in Bavaria, Baden-Württemberg, and Saxony-Anhalt. Children dress as the Three Kings and carol through neighbourhoods.
International Rubber Ducky Day on January 13 honours the iconic rubber duck toy, a beloved bath companion for children worldwide. It was created by Ernie's famous bathtub song on Sesame Street.
Winnie the Pooh Day is celebrated on January 18, the birthday of A. A. Milne, creator of the beloved bear. It is a day to enjoy the simple joys, share honey, and live by the philosophy of Pooh.

slogans.en: A day without a friend is like a pot without a single drop of honey.

descriptions.en: Popcorn Day on January 19 celebrates the beloved snack that has been enjoyed since ancient times. Whether sweet, salty, or caramel, popcorn is the perfect companion for movies and gatherings.

Proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly, this day celebrates education's role in peace and development. Education is the foundation of sustainable development and a basic human right for everyone.

slogans.en: Education is a right, not a privilege.

descriptions.en: National Peanut Butter Day on January 24 is a celebration of the beloved American spread. Peanut butter is enjoyed worldwide on sandwiches, in desserts, and straight from the jar.

slogans.en: Smooth or Crunchy — Just Love Peanut Butter!

descriptions.en: Australia Day is the official national day of Australia and commemorates the arrival of the First Fleet at Port Jackson, New South Wales, in 1788. It is celebrated with community events, citizenship ceremonies, and Australia Day honors.

India Republic Day on January 26 commemorates the date when the Constitution of India came into effect in 1950, replacing the Government of India Act as the governing document. A grand parade is held at New Delhi's Rajpath.

This day marks the anniversary of the liberation of Auschwitz-Birkenau, the largest Nazi concentration and extermination camp. It is a day to remember the six million Jewish victims and millions of others killed by the Nazi regime.

Data Privacy Day raises awareness about the importance of respecting privacy, safeguarding data, and enabling trust in our increasingly connected world. It empowers people and organizations to take action to protect personal data.

Chinese New Year (Spring Festival) is the most important traditional holiday in China, celebrated by Chinese communities worldwide. The date varies each year based on the lunar calendar, typically falling between January 21 and February 20.

slogans.en: Gong Xi Fa Cai — Wishing You Prosperity!

descriptions.en: National Hot Chocolate Day on January 31 celebrates the warm, comforting beverage loved by millions. It's the perfect day to curl up with a steaming mug of hot chocolate.

slogans.en: Warm Your Soul with Every Sip

descriptions.en: World Hijab Day was founded by Nazma Khan in 2013 to foster religious tolerance and understanding. Women of all faiths and backgrounds are invited to wear the hijab for a day to experience life in a headscarf.

World Wetlands Day marks the date of the adoption of the Ramsar Convention in 1971. It aims to raise awareness about the vital role wetlands play for people and planet — from freshwater supply to biodiversity and climate regulation.
Groundhog Day on February 2 is a popular tradition in North America where a groundhog named Punxsutawney Phil emerges from its burrow. If it sees its shadow, six more weeks of winter are predicted.

World Cancer Day unites the world's population in the fight against cancer. Led by the Union for International Cancer Control, it aims to save millions of preventable deaths each year by raising awareness and education about cancer.

World Nutella Day was created in 2007 by Sara Rosso, an American Nutella fan who blogged about her love of the chocolate-hazelnut spread. It's a day to celebrate and share the joy of Nutella with the world.

Waitangi Day on February 6 is New Zealand's national day. It celebrates the anniversary of the signing of the Treaty of Waitangi in 1840, which established the relationship between the Crown and Māori.

slogans.en: He iwi tahi tātou — We are one people.

descriptions.en: National Pizza Day on February 9 is a celebration of one of the world's most beloved foods. Pizza lovers everywhere indulge in their favorite slices and explore new flavors.

names.en: International Day of Women and Girls in Science

descriptions.en: Established by the United Nations, this day recognizes the critical role women and girls play in science and technology. It promotes full and equal access to and participation in science for women and girls.

National Foundation Day on February 11 commemorates the founding of Japan by its first Emperor Jimmu in 660 BC. It is a public holiday for Japanese people to reflect on the history and culture of their nation.

Red Hand Day (International Day Against the Use of Child Soldiers) is observed on February 12 to raise awareness about child soldiers and draw attention to the need for greater action to end this practice worldwide.

slogans.en: No child should be a soldier.

descriptions.en: Darwin Day celebrates the birthday of Charles Darwin (born February 12, 1809) and promotes awareness about science and humanity. Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection revolutionized our understanding of life on Earth.

World Radio Day celebrates radio as a medium and improves international cooperation between broadcasters. Radio reaches the widest audience of any medium and touches all aspects of human life including culture, entertainment, and education.

Valentine's Day is a celebration of love and affection between intimate companions. Observed on February 14, it is celebrated in many countries around the world with exchanging gifts, flowers, and heartfelt messages.

Legacy Week is Australia's annual tribute to the families of military personnel who lost their lives or health in service, anchored by Legacy — an organization founded by Captain Stanley Savige in Melbourne in 1923 to care for the widows and children of his fallen comrades. The week honours service and sacrifice through memorial services like the Memorial Day Wreath Ceremony on the USS Midway, fundraising appeals, movie nights celebrating heroes, memory walls, charity bake sales, community picnics and storytelling evenings with veterans. Legacy supports over 43,000 beneficiaries annually, with the Legacy badge symbolising mateship, compassion and fairness.

slogans.en: Keep the promise. Carry their light.

descriptions.en: National Beach Day, founded in 2014 by animal activist and lifestyle expert Colleen Paige, is a call to clean the places we love most. Beaches nourish millions of outdoor memories — swimming, surfing, sandcastles, picnics, and quiet mornings — yet they degrade under pollution and climate pressure. The day invites everyone to do their part: grab a bag and a few friends, join or organize a beach cleanup, support groups like Surfrider Foundation, Oceana or The Nature Conservancy, and help keep our coastlines beautiful and sustainable for generations to come.

National Grief Awareness Day, founded by Angela Cartwright, honors the reality that grief is part of life — a response to losing someone or something we love. It exists to remind us how to be there for others: presence over advice, listening over fixing. The day talks about the well-known five stages — denial, anger, bargaining, depression, acceptance — not as a linear path but as a loop we move through differently in every moment. The invitation is simple: be there. Bring a meal, lend an ear, share a laugh, or just sit.

We Love Memoirs Day was founded in 2013 by memoir authors Victoria Twead and Alan Parks to bring readers and writers together around one of literature's most intimate forms. A memoir focuses on a single, significant period or moment rather than the whole sweep of a life — The Diary of a Young Girl by Anne Frank is perhaps the most famous example. The day is celebrated with online writing circles, where new memoirists pick up tips, make friends and share drafts; by starting a personal memoir of one's own; and simply by recommending a favourite memoir to someone who hasn't read it.

slogans.en: Every life hides a story worth telling.

descriptions.en: National Eat Outside Day celebrates the oldest trick in the human playbook — taking the meal outdoors. The tradition stretches back centuries: medieval hunters packed provisions for the trail, Bavarian beer gardens opened in the 17th century, picnics caught on in 18th-century American 'pleasure gardens,' and Charles Feltman's Coney Island sausage sandwich birthed the hot dog in 1884. The day invites a picnic in the park, a few friends around a backyard grill, a patio table at a favourite restaurant — any excuse to skip the dining room while the weather still cooperates.

slogans.en: Eat outside. That's the whole rule.

descriptions.en: National Matchmaker Day was founded in 2016 by jewellery house ArtCarved Bridal to honour the people — professional or amateur — who spend their lives putting others in the same room and hoping something sparks. Matchmakers pre-screen for compatibility in ways no app can match, and they carry awkward conversations and fragile confidence for their clients. The day is a low-stakes chance to thank whoever set you up, play Cupid between two single friends, host a mixer, or share your own love story inspired by someone else's match.

slogans.en: Cupid called. He's on a coffee run.

descriptions.en: World Distance Learning Day celebrates the freedom to learn without borders. Its roots go back further than the internet: in 1728 Caleb Phillips taught shorthand by mail in Boston; in the 1840s Isaac Pitman taught the same subject by postcard; in 1858 the University of London became the first to grant degrees to remote students. Radio, television and the internet each widened access further — and distance learning now lets parents, night-shift workers and rural learners study on their own schedule, at any hour. The day invites trying a free online class, sharing what you learned, helping someone start a course, or joining a virtual study group.

names.en: International Day for People of African Descent

descriptions.en: The International Day for People of African Descent was established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2020 and first observed in 2021. It rests on three principles — recognition, justice, and development — and asks the world to confront the centuries of injustice that people of African descent have endured: the Transatlantic slave trade, colonial rule, and the ongoing discrimination and systemic racism that shape justice systems today. The day invites joining community events, reading books and watching documentaries about the African diaspora, standing up against inequity, and supporting organisations working on education and legal aid.
World Pangolin Day on the third Saturday of February is a day to raise awareness about pangolins, the world's most trafficked wild mammals.

slogans.en: Protecting the World's Most Trafficked Mammal

descriptions.en: Parinirvana Day (February 15) is a Buddhist holiday marking the death of Gautama Buddha at the age of 80, and his attainment of complete Nirvana. Buddhists meditate, read scriptures, and gather at temples to reflect on Buddha's teachings.

slogans.en: Peace in stillness, light in darkness.

descriptions.en: Random Acts of Kindness Day on February 17 encourages people to perform selfless acts of kindness for others, whether friends, family, or complete strangers. Small acts can have enormous ripple effects.

slogans.en: One Small Act. One Big Impact.

descriptions.en: The World Day of Social Justice is an international day recognizing the need to promote social justice, which includes efforts to tackle issues such as poverty, exclusion, gender inequality, unemployment, and human rights.

slogans.en: Achieving Social Justice for a Fair Globalization.

descriptions.en: International Mother Language Day promotes linguistic and cultural diversity and multilingualism. It has been observed globally since 2000. About half of the estimated 6,000 languages spoken in the world are in danger of disappearing.

Estonia's Independence Day on February 24 commemorates the Declaration of Independence of 1918. Having restored independence from the Soviet Union in 1991, Estonia celebrates its freedom and democratic values.
World Pancake Day (Shrove Tuesday / Pancake Tuesday) is celebrated the day before Ash Wednesday, with people making and eating pancakes to use up rich ingredients before Lent.

slogans.en: Flip for Joy — It's Pancake Day!

descriptions.en: Pokémon Day on February 27 celebrates the anniversary of the release of the original Pokémon Red and Green games in Japan in 1996. Fans worldwide celebrate their love for the iconic franchise.
National Science Day in India is celebrated on February 28 to mark the discovery of the Raman Effect by Indian physicist C.V. Raman in 1928.
Zero Discrimination Day is celebrated every year on 1 March to promote equality before the law and in practice throughout all of the member countries. The butterfly is the symbol of the day.

slogans.en: End inequalities. End AIDS. End pandemics.

descriptions.en: World Compliment Day on March 1 is the world's most positive day. The idea originated in the Netherlands in 2001 and spread globally. The challenge: give at least three people a sincere, personal compliment.
St. David's Day is the feast day of Saint David, the patron saint of Wales, celebrated on March 1 with festivals, daffodils, and Welsh cultural pride.
International Wheelchair Day celebrates the positive impact a wheelchair has on the lives of users, and enables wheelchair users around the world to share their experiences of using a wheelchair.

slogans.en: Rolling through life with strength and pride.

descriptions.en: World Wildlife Day is the most important global annual event dedicated to wild animals and plants. It celebrates the variety of wild fauna and flora and raises awareness of the many benefits that conservation provides to people.

slogans.en: Caring for all life on Earth.

descriptions.en: World Hearing Day is held each year on 3 March to raise awareness on how to prevent deafness and hearing loss and promote ear and hearing care across the world. Over 1.5 billion people live with hearing loss globally.

slogans.en: Hearing for life — don't let hearing loss limit you.

descriptions.en: Ghana's Independence Day on March 6 marks the day in 1957 when Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from British colonial rule. The historic event inspired independence movements across Africa.
World Day of Prayer is an international ecumenical movement of Christian women who invite all people to observe a day of prayer and action for peace and justice.

slogans.en: Together in Prayer for a Peaceful World

descriptions.en: International Women's Day is a global day celebrating the social, economic, cultural, and political achievements of women. The day also marks a call to action for accelerating gender parity worldwide.

World Glaucoma Day is dedicated to raising awareness about glaucoma, the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. Early detection and treatment are key to preventing vision loss from this silent thief of sight.

slogans.en: Beat invisible glaucoma — get your eyes checked.

descriptions.en: Pi Day is an annual celebration of the mathematical constant π (pi). It is observed on March 14 since 3, 1, and 4 are the first three significant digits of π. It's also Albert Einstein's birthday!
The International Day of Mathematics is celebrated on March 14 (Pi Day) to promote the beauty and importance of mathematics in human progress.

names.en: International Day of Action for Rivers

descriptions.en: The International Day of Action for Rivers unites people worldwide to celebrate rivers and advocate for their protection. Rivers provide freshwater for billions, support biodiversity, and sustain entire civilizations.

World Consumer Rights Day is an opportunity to promote the basic rights of all consumers, demand that those rights are respected and protected, and protest against market abuses and social injustices which undermine those rights.
World Sleep Day is an annual event, typically on the Friday before the March vernal equinox. It promotes healthy sleep through education, awareness, and management of sleep disorders.

World Speech Day celebrates the power of speech to inspire, unite, and change the world. It focuses on speech as a fundamental human skill and promotes speech therapy awareness for those with communication disorders.

slogans.en: Speak up, speak out, change the world.

descriptions.en: Saint Patrick's Day is a cultural and religious celebration held on the death date of Saint Patrick, the foremost patron saint of Ireland. It celebrates Irish culture with parades, special foods, music, dancing, and a whole lot of green.

slogans.en: Everybody's Irish on St. Patrick's Day.

descriptions.en: The International Day of Happiness recognizes that the pursuit of happiness is a fundamental human goal. The UN encourages 193 member states to consider happiness in their policies and measure national well-being.

World Sparrow Day is observed on March 20 to raise awareness of the house sparrow and other common birds threatened by urbanization. House sparrow populations have declined dramatically in many urban areas worldwide.
World Oral Health Day raises awareness of the importance of good oral hygiene and its link to overall health, as well as the prevention of oral diseases.
World Storytelling Day celebrates the art of oral storytelling. People around the world gather to share stories and keep ancient traditions alive.

slogans.en: Every Story Deserves to Be Heard

descriptions.en: French Language Day (March 20) is celebrated on the anniversary of the creation of the Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie. It promotes the French language and Francophone cultures worldwide. French is spoken by 300 million people.
World Poetry Day celebrates one of humanity's most treasured forms of cultural and linguistic expression and identity. Poetry gives voice to our common humanity with all its complexity and diversity.

slogans.en: Poetry: the art of being human.

descriptions.en: The International Day of Forests celebrates and raises awareness of the importance of all types of forests for the benefit of current and future generations. Forests are the lungs of our Earth.

slogans.en: Forests and sustainable production and consumption.

descriptions.en: World Down Syndrome Day is a global awareness day to advocate for the rights, inclusion, and well-being of people with Down syndrome. The date 21/3 was chosen to signify the triplication (trisomy) of the 21st chromosome.
Nowruz is the Persian New Year, celebrated by millions of people on the vernal equinox around March 21, marking the beginning of spring and renewal.

World Puppetry Day (March 21) was established by the Union Internationale de la Marionnette in 2003. It celebrates puppetry as one of humanity's oldest art forms used for storytelling, ritual, and entertainment across all cultures.

slogans.en: Pull the strings — tell the story.

descriptions.en: World Water Day is an annual United Nations observance day that highlights the importance of freshwater. The day is used to advocate for the sustainable management of freshwater resources.
Earth Hour is a worldwide movement organized by WWF where people and businesses turn off non-essential electric lights for one hour to raise awareness about climate change.
World Taxi Day on March 22 honors taxi drivers worldwide — the unsung heroes who navigate cities day and night, keeping millions of people moving safely.

World Meteorological Day commemorates the establishment of the World Meteorological Organization on 23 March 1950. It celebrates the role of meteorology in keeping people safe and sustaining the environment.
World Puppy Day, founded in 2006 by animal advocate Colleen Paige, celebrates the joy puppies bring to our lives and raises awareness about adoption and responsible pet ownership.

World TB Day, observed on March 24, marks the date Dr Robert Koch announced the discovery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in 1882. It is dedicated to raising awareness about TB and mobilizing resources to combat the disease.
Greek Independence Day on March 25 commemorates the start of the War of Independence against the Ottoman Empire in 1821. Military parades are held across Greece, with the largest in Athens.

Tolkien Reading Day (March 25) encourages fans around the world to celebrate the life and work of J.R.R. Tolkien, author of The Lord of the Rings. March 25 marks the date on which the One Ring was destroyed in the fires of Mount Doom.

slogans.en: Not all those who wander are lost.

descriptions.en: Bangladesh Independence Day on March 26 commemorates the declaration of independence from Pakistan in 1971. Bangladesh also celebrates Liberation Day (Victory Day) on December 16 marking the end of the Liberation War.

Purple Day is an international epilepsy awareness day founded by nine-year-old Cassidy Megan from Nova Scotia in 2008. People around the world are encouraged to wear purple and talk about epilepsy to dispel myths.

slogans.en: Wear purple. Stand up for epilepsy awareness.

descriptions.en: World Theatre Day was initiated in 1961 by the International Theatre Institute. It is celebrated on the 27th of March each year by ITI Centres and the international theatre community.

slogans.en: Theatre and a culture of peace.

descriptions.en: World Piano Day falls on the 88th day of the year (March 29) — matching the number of keys on a piano. Founded by pianist Nils Frahm in 2015, it celebrates the piano and encourages people of all ages to sit down and play.
World Bipolar Day is observed on the birthday of Vincent Van Gogh, who is believed to have had bipolar disorder. The day works to eliminate social stigma and brings world awareness to this condition.
World Backup Day on March 31 was created as a reminder to back up all your important files before April Fool's Day on April 1. It is a tech community initiative to promote data protection habits.

slogans.en: Don't be an April Fool. Backup Your Files!

descriptions.en: International Transgender Day of Visibility (TDOV) is an annual event dedicated to celebrating transgender and gender non-conforming people and raising awareness of discrimination faced by transgender people worldwide.

April Fools' Day, also called All Fools' Day, is celebrated on April 1 each year. People play practical jokes and hoaxes on each other and then shout 'April Fools!' The origins of this playful tradition remain a mystery.

slogans.en: Don't believe everything you read today.

descriptions.en: World Autism Awareness Day is a United Nations sanctioned day to promote awareness of people with autism spectrum disorder. More than 1 in 100 children worldwide has autism.

International Children's Book Day (ICBD) is observed on Hans Christian Andersen's birthday, April 2, to inspire a love of reading and to call attention to children's books. It is celebrated by the International Board on Books for Young People.

slogans.en: Every child deserves a great book.

descriptions.en: International Fact-Checking Day promotes the importance of fact-checking in an era of misinformation. Held on April 2 (the day after April Fool's Day), it encourages critical thinking, media literacy, and the verification of claims.

slogans.en: Don't get fooled — check the facts.

descriptions.en: World Party Day on April 3 encourages people to celebrate life, connect with others, and simply have fun. It was inspired by the 1997 novel 'Flight: A Trilogy' and has since grown into an international celebration.
International Boxing Day on April 5 celebrates the sport of boxing worldwide, honoring the discipline, skill, and dedication of boxers from amateur to professional levels.

slogans.en: Float Like a Butterfly, Sting Like a Bee

descriptions.en: World Health Day is a global health awareness day celebrated every year on April 7, under the sponsorship of the World Health Organization. It marks the founding of WHO in 1948.

World Parkinson's Day raises awareness about Parkinson's disease, a progressive neurological disorder affecting millions worldwide. It honors Dr. James Parkinson who first described the disease on this date in 1817 and supports those living with the condition.
Yuri's Night celebrates the anniversary of the first human spaceflight by Yuri Gagarin on April 12, 1961. The day also coincides with the first launch of the Space Shuttle in 1981.

slogans.en: The universe is yours to explore.

descriptions.en: World Space Day on April 12 marks the anniversary of Yuri Gagarin's first human space flight in 1961. It is a day to celebrate humanity's achievements in space exploration and inspire the next generation of explorers.

Baisakhi (Vaisakhi) is a harvest festival celebrated in the Punjab region of India and Pakistan. It also marks the Sikh New Year and commemorates the formation of the Khalsa Panth in 1699 by Guru Gobind Singh.

slogans.en: Harvest, heritage, and the spirit of Khalsa.

descriptions.en: World Art Day on April 15 promotes the development, diffusion, and enjoyment of art. The date was chosen to celebrate the birthday of Leonardo da Vinci, who is considered a symbol of peace, freedom of expression, tolerance, and fraternity.

slogans.en: Art Speaks Where Words Are Unable to Explain.

descriptions.en: World Hemophilia Day raises awareness about hemophilia and other inherited bleeding disorders. It advocates for access to care for millions of people with bleeding disorders globally who often lack adequate treatment.

slogans.en: Treatment for all — no one left behind.

descriptions.en: International Haiku Poetry Day celebrates the Japanese art form of haiku poetry — three-line poems capturing a moment in nature and human experience. Haiku has spread worldwide and is practiced in many languages.

World Heritage Day (International Day for Monuments and Sites) promotes awareness about the diversity of cultural heritage and the efforts required to protect and conserve them. UNESCO inscribes over 1,100 sites of outstanding universal value.

slogans.en: Heritage is our legacy from the past, what we live with today, and what we pass on to future generations.

descriptions.en: World Cycling Day on April 19 promotes cycling as a sustainable mode of transport and a sport for all ages. Cycling benefits individual health and reduces carbon emissions, making it a win for people and the planet.
World Creativity and Innovation Day on April 21 encourages people to use new ideas, novel solutions, and creative approaches to address the challenges of sustainable development.

Earth Day is an annual event on April 22 to demonstrate support for environmental protection. First held in 1970, it now includes a wide range of events coordinated globally, including 1 billion people in more than 193 countries.

World Book and Copyright Day celebrates books and reading, and is marked in over 100 countries. The date was chosen because it is the anniversary of the death of William Shakespeare and Miguel de Cervantes.

slogans.en: Read, so you never have to stop traveling.

descriptions.en: National Sovereignty and Children's Day in Turkey commemorates the opening of the Grand National Assembly on April 23, 1920, and is also dedicated to children. It is the first holiday in the world dedicated entirely to children.

St George's Day on April 23 is the feast day of Saint George, the patron saint of England. It celebrates English culture, heritage, and identity, though it is less widely celebrated than other national days.

names.en: World Day for Animals in Laboratories

descriptions.en: World Day for Animals in Laboratories promotes the end of animal testing and the development of humane alternatives. Over 100 million animals are used in experiments worldwide each year, raising ethical questions about animal rights in scientific research.
World Malaria Day, observed on April 25 each year, is a day for recognizing global efforts to control malaria. Malaria is preventable and treatable yet still kills hundreds of thousands each year.
World Penguin Day on April 25 was started by researchers at the US Antarctic research station McMurdo who noticed penguins tended to return from their winter migration north on this date.

ANZAC Day on April 25 is a national day of remembrance in Australia and New Zealand that broadly commemorates all Australians and New Zealanders who served and died in all wars, conflicts, and peacekeeping operations.

World Intellectual Property Day on April 26 is dedicated to raising awareness about how patents, copyright, trademarks and designs impact everyday life. It celebrates the innovations and creative works that enrich the world.

slogans.en: IP and You: Driving a Better Future.

descriptions.en: King's Day (Koningsdag) on April 27 celebrates the birthday of King Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands. The entire country turns orange — the national colour — and people celebrate with outdoor markets, concerts, and boat parades.

Freedom Day in South Africa on April 27 commemorates the first democratic elections held on that date in 1994, when all South Africans were able to vote for the first time, marking the end of apartheid.

International Dance Day was created in 1982 by the Dance Committee of the International Theatre Institute. It celebrates dance as a universal language that transcends all political, cultural, and ethnic barriers.

slogans.en: Dance is an art that imprints on the soul.

descriptions.en: Golden Week in Japan is a collection of four national holidays within one week from late April to early May. It is one of Japan's biggest holiday periods when many travel and celebrate.

International Jazz Day highlights jazz and its diplomatic role of uniting people in all corners of the globe. Proclaimed by UNESCO in 2011, it brings together communities and schools around the world through music education.

Walpurgis Night (April 30) is a traditional spring festival celebrated in Germany, Sweden, and Finland. Named after Saint Walpurga, it features bonfires, folk music, dancing, and the driving away of evil spirits to welcome the season of light.

slogans.en: Dance around the bonfire — spring has arrived!

descriptions.en: International Workers' Day, also known as Labour Day or May Day, is a celebration of laborers and the working classes. It commemorates the Haymarket affair of 1886 and the eight-hour workday movement.

slogans.en: Workers united will never be defeated.

descriptions.en: Labour and Solidarity Day is a public holiday in Turkey celebrated on May 1. While workers' movements had observed this date since the early 20th century, it was officially recognised as a national holiday in Turkey in 2009. The day honours the contributions of workers and trade unions and is marked with rallies and events across the country.

slogans.en: Labour is the foundation of dignity.

descriptions.en: No Meat May is a global month-long initiative encouraging people to go meat-free throughout May. Started in Australia in 2013 with just 30 friends, it has grown to over 130,000 participants worldwide. The challenge supports healthier bodies, a lower carbon footprint, and a more sustainable food system.

slogans.en: One month. No meat. Massive impact.

descriptions.en: National Photography Month every May celebrates photography as art, communication, and memory. Officially recognized by the US Congress in 1987, the medium itself dates back to 1826 when Joseph Nicéphore Niépce captured the world's first permanent photograph. Use this month to take more photos, visit galleries, or learn a new technique.

slogans.en: Every photo tells a story worth keeping.

descriptions.en: World Tuna Day was established by the United Nations in 2017. Tuna are a vital part of our ocean ecosystem and global food security. Over 7 million tonnes of tuna are consumed globally each year.

World Press Freedom Day reminds governments of their duty to respect and uphold the right to freedom of expression. It also celebrates the fundamental principles of press freedom and defends media from attacks on its independence.

slogans.en: A press for the planet: journalism in the face of the environmental crisis.

descriptions.en: Star Wars Day is an unofficial fan holiday celebrating the Star Wars film franchise. The date comes from a pun on the Jedi greeting 'May the Force be with you' — 'May the Fourth be with you.'
World Laughter Day is celebrated on the first Sunday of May. It was created in 1998 by Dr Madan Kataria, founder of the Laughter Yoga movement, to promote world peace through laughter and joy.
Mother's Day is a celebration honoring mothers and celebrating motherhood, maternal bonds, and the influence of mothers in society. It is celebrated on the second Sunday in May in many countries.

slogans.en: Celebrating the Heart of Every Home

descriptions.en: World Drone Day celebrates unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) and their incredible applications in photography, delivery, disaster relief, and exploration.

slogans.en: The Sky is Not the Limit

descriptions.en: Anti-Bullying Day raises awareness about bullying in schools and online, encouraging everyone to stand up for those being bullied. Bullying affects millions of children worldwide and has serious impacts on mental health.

slogans.en: Stand up, speak out, stop bullying.

descriptions.en: Cinco de Mayo, or the 5th of May, commemorates the Mexican Army's victory over the French Empire at the Battle of Puebla in 1862. It is widely celebrated in Mexico and the United States.
International No Diet Day on May 6 promotes body acceptance, healthy lifestyles, and awareness of the harms of diet culture and weight discrimination.

slogans.en: Your body is beautiful — no diet needed.

descriptions.en: World Athletics Day is celebrated on May 7 and was established by World Athletics (formerly IAAF) to promote track and field sports among young people and inspire them to lead active lives.

slogans.en: Run, Jump, Throw: Athletics for All.

names.en: World Red Cross and Red Crescent Day

descriptions.en: World Red Cross and Red Crescent Day is observed on May 8 to commemorate the birthday of Henry Dunant, founder of the International Committee of the Red Cross. The day honors volunteers and staff who save lives around the world.

slogans.en: Everything we do starts with humanity.

descriptions.en: World Ovarian Cancer Day unites the global ovarian cancer community in raising awareness about the disease and its symptoms. Early detection saves lives — knowing the signs is crucial for survival.
Europe Day celebrates peace and unity in Europe on May 9 each year. The date is the anniversary of the Schuman Declaration, which was the beginning of what is now the European Union.
World Migratory Bird Day is an annual awareness-raising campaign highlighting the need for conservation of migratory birds and their habitats.

World Lupus Day calls on governments and public health officials to improve healthcare services for lupus patients and increase investment in lupus research. Lupus is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting millions globally.
International Nurses Day is celebrated worldwide on May 12, the anniversary of Florence Nightingale's birth, to mark the contributions that nurses make to society.

slogans.en: Nurses: A Voice to Lead — Health for All

descriptions.en: Vesak Day, also known as Buddha Day, honors the birth, enlightenment, and passing into Nirvana of Siddhartha Gautama. Observed on the full moon of the Vaisakha lunar month — usually in May — it is the most sacred day in the Buddhist calendar. Millions mark it with meditation, temple visits, lantern releases, and acts of compassion. The UN officially recognized it as an international day in 1999.

slogans.en: May all beings be happy and free.

descriptions.en: May 14 is Scientific Pharmacy Day in Turkey, celebrating the pharmacist's role as a healthcare professional grounded in science. The date commemorates the founding of the first modern school of pharmacy in Turkey. Pharmacists across the country are recognised for their contributions to public health, medication safety, and evidence-based practice.

May 14 is Farmers' Day in Turkey, honouring the farmers and agricultural workers who feed the nation. The date was chosen to mark the anniversary of Turkey's first general elections held on May 14, 1950 — a milestone driven largely by the rural farming population. The day recognises the vital role of agriculture in Turkey's economy, culture, and food security.

Israel Independence Day (Yom Ha'atzmaut) celebrates the proclamation of independence on May 14, 1948, when David Ben-Gurion announced the establishment of the State of Israel. The date on the Hebrew calendar varies annually.

slogans.en: Am Yisrael Chai! (The People of Israel Live!)

descriptions.en: The International Day of Families provides an opportunity to promote awareness of issues relating to families and to increase knowledge of the social, economic and demographic processes affecting them.

slogans.en: Families and climate action: focus on SDGs.

descriptions.en: The International Day Against Homophobia, Transphobia and Biphobia is observed on May 17 to raise awareness of LGBT+ rights violations and stimulate interest in LGBT+ rights work. May 17 marks the day homosexuality was removed from the WHO classification of diseases in 1990.

slogans.en: Our bodies, our lives, our rights.

descriptions.en: Norway's Constitution Day (Syttende mai) on May 17 commemorates the signing of the Norwegian Constitution in 1814. It is Norway's most important national holiday, celebrated with children's parades and traditional bunad costumes.
Endangered Species Day is a day to learn about and celebrate the rare and endangered species that share our planet, and the efforts to protect them.

International Museum Day takes place on or around May 18 each year. It aims to raise awareness of the fact that museums are an important means of cultural exchange, enrichment of cultures and development of mutual understanding, cooperation and peace.

The AIDS Candlelight Memorial, observed on the third Sunday of May, is the oldest and largest community-based HIV/AIDS awareness event in the world. It honours those who have died of AIDS and supports people living with HIV.

slogans.en: Light a Candle. Honour a Life.

names.en: Atatürk Commemoration, Youth and Sports Day (Turkey)

descriptions.en: May 19 commemorates Mustafa Kemal Atatürk's arrival in Samsun in 1919, which marked the beginning of the Turkish War of Independence. The day is also dedicated to the youth of Turkey and to sports, reflecting Atatürk's famous quote entrusting the nation's future to its young people. It is celebrated with youth festivals, athletic events, and ceremonies across the country.

slogans.en: Muhtaç olduğun kudret, damarlarındaki asil kanda mevcuttur.

descriptions.en: Malcolm X Day honors the birthday of Malcolm X (born May 19, 1925), a prominent civil rights leader and Black nationalist who advocated for the rights of African Americans and the empowerment of Black communities.

slogans.en: By any means necessary — stand for justice.

descriptions.en: World Bee Day aims to raise awareness of the importance of bees and other pollinators for our ecosystem and food supply. Around 75% of food crops worldwide depend on pollinators.

World Tea Day on May 21 was established by the UN Food and Agriculture Organization to promote sustainable tea production and raise awareness of the cultural and economic significance of tea worldwide.

World Fish Migration Day raises global awareness about the importance of open rivers and migratory fish. Dams, weirs, and pollution block fish migration routes, threatening many species with extinction.

slogans.en: Open rivers, migratory fish — a healthy planet.

descriptions.en: The International Day for Biological Diversity promotes awareness and understanding of biodiversity issues. Biodiversity is the foundation of life on Earth — healthy ecosystems clean water, purify air, maintain soil, regulate climate, and provide resources for human survival.

Bitcoin Pizza Day (May 22) marks the date in 2010 when Laszlo Hanyecz made the first real-world Bitcoin transaction, buying two pizzas for 10,000 BTC. This landmark event is celebrated in the crypto community as the birth of Bitcoin commerce.

slogans.en: The most expensive pizzas in history.

descriptions.en: On May 23, 1949, the Basic Law (Grundgesetz) — the constitution of the Federal Republic of Germany — was promulgated, laying the foundation for a democratic, federal state. Shaped by the lessons of the Nazi era, the Grundgesetz enshrines fundamental rights as inviolable and directly binding on all state authority. It is considered one of the most successful constitutions in history.
World Turtle Day, sponsored annually by American Tortoise Rescue, is a day to help people celebrate and protect turtles and tortoises.

Towel Day is celebrated as a tribute to the late Douglas Adams, author of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. Fans carry a towel on this day in honour of the most important item an interstellar hitchhiker can have.

slogans.en: Don't panic. And carry a towel.

descriptions.en: World Football Day on May 25 commemorates the first international football match ever held in 1924 at the Paris Olympics. It is a day to celebrate the world's most popular sport.

slogans.en: The Beautiful Game Belongs to Everyone.

descriptions.en: World Otter Day raises awareness about the threats facing otters worldwide. All 13 otter species face varying levels of threat from habitat loss, pollution, hunting, and illegal trade. Otters are vital ecosystem engineers.

Geek Pride Day (May 25) celebrates geek culture and encourages everyone to embrace their inner geek. May 25 was chosen to coincide with the release of Star Wars in 1977 and Towel Day (Hitchhiker's Guide) — two beloved geek touchstones.

slogans.en: Be proud to be a geek!

descriptions.en: World Hamburger Day on May 28 is a global celebration of the world's most popular sandwich. Whether beef, chicken, veggie, or gourmet, the hamburger is enjoyed by billions of people daily.

slogans.en: Grill It. Stack It. Devour It.

descriptions.en: World No Tobacco Day is observed around the world every year on May 31. This initiative by the World Health Organization informs the public on the dangers of using tobacco and calls on countries to implement effective policies to reduce tobacco consumption.

National Smile Day on May 31 was established in 2018 by dentists Dr. Tim Stirneman and Jim Wojdyla to celebrate the power of a smile. Science backs it up: smiling releases endorphins, reduces stress, and can even lower blood pressure. Today, share your smile with the world.

World Parrot Day on May 31 was established in 2004 by the World Parrot Trust to celebrate these remarkable birds and raise awareness about their conservation. Many parrot species are threatened by deforestation, illegal trade, and habitat destruction. Today, learn about their intelligence, beauty, and vital role in forest ecosystems.

slogans.en: Protect the world's most colorful voices.

descriptions.en: World Foster Day on May 31 raises awareness about foster care and the children who cannot safely remain with their families. Established in 2018, it celebrates foster parents, social workers, educators, and mentors while amplifying the voices of those with lived experience in care. The day advocates for family-based solutions over institutional care.

slogans.en: Every child deserves a safe place to call home.

descriptions.en: African American Music Appreciation Month, celebrated every June, honors the profound contributions of Black musicians across jazz, gospel, rhythm and blues, and hip-hop. Founded in 1979 by President Jimmy Carter at the urging of songwriter Kenny Gamble, it was renamed by President Barack Obama in 2009 to reflect its broader significance. From Louis Armstrong to Beyoncé, Black artists have shaped the sound of American culture and driven global music movements.

slogans.en: The music that moved the world.

descriptions.en: International Children's Day is celebrated on June 1 in many countries. It was first proclaimed at the World Conference for the Well-being of Children in Geneva in 1925. The day recognizes children's rights and promotes their welfare.

slogans.en: Every child has the right to a happy childhood.

descriptions.en: World Milk Day was established by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations in 2001 to recognize the importance of milk as a global food, and to celebrate the dairy sector. It is observed internationally on June 1.
The Global Day of Parents is observed on June 1 each year. It provides an opportunity to appreciate all parents in all parts of the world for their selfless commitment to children.

Pride Month is celebrated every June to honor the LGBTQ+ community and commemorate the Stonewall Riots of June 1969 — a pivotal moment in the fight for LGBTQ+ rights. The month is marked by parades, festivals, marches, and educational events around the world, celebrating love, identity, and equality.

slogans.en: Love is love — every color of the rainbow.

descriptions.en: National Adopt a Cat Month, observed every June, encourages people to open their homes to cats in shelters. Founded in 1998 by the American Humane Association, the campaign highlights that millions of cats enter shelters each year — June being peak kitten season — making it the perfect time to give a feline a forever home.

slogans.en: Give a cat a forever home.

descriptions.en: National Olive Day is celebrated on June 1, wrapping up Mediterranean Diet Month in the United States. Established in 2015 by Divina, a specialty Mediterranean foods company, it honors the olive — one of humanity’s oldest cultivated fruits with a 6,000-year heritage. Olives are technically stone fruits, and with roughly 500 varieties worldwide, they remain a cornerstone of healthy Mediterranean cuisine, from brined table olives to extra-virgin olive oil.

Wear a Dress Day takes place every June 1, born in Bend, Oregon in 2010 when a group of women decided to champion the joy of wearing dresses. Word spread through social media and the celebration attracted over 100,000 participants in its very first year. The day is open to everyone regardless of gender — it's simply an invitation to embrace self-expression and a little extra fun in getting dressed.

slogans.en: Wear it, feel it, own it.

descriptions.en: Say Something Nice Day is observed on June 1, originating in Charleston, South Carolina in 2006 when Mayor Keith Summey proclaimed it in honor of Dr. Mitch Carnell, author of 'Say Something Nice: Be a Lifter at Work.' Created to counter workplace negativity, the day champions sincere compliments and kind words. Science backs it up: genuine praise activates the same brain reward circuits as receiving money, and positively communicating teams consistently outperform those that don't.

slogans.en: Kind words cost nothing and mean everything.

descriptions.en: Dinosaur Day on June 1 celebrates the prehistoric giants that ruled Earth for over 180 million years. Humanity's fascination with dinosaurs dates to 1677, when Oxford professor Robert Plot discovered the first fossil bone — though he mistook it for a giant human's. It wasn't until 1842 that Sir Richard Owen coined the term 'Dinosauria' (meaning 'terrible lizard'). Today, birds are recognized as living theropod dinosaurs, meaning dinosaurs never truly went extinct.

slogans.en: Millions of years gone, never forgotten.

descriptions.en: Italian Republic Day on June 2 commemorates the 1946 referendum when Italians chose a republic over a monarchy. The day is celebrated with a military parade in Rome and official ceremonies across the country.

Leave the Office Earlier Day encourages employees to wrap up their tasks efficiently and head home early. Founded by productivity expert Laura Stack, the day is a reminder that working smarter — not longer — leads to better results and a healthier work-life balance.

World Bicycle Day recognizes the uniqueness, longevity, and versatility of the bicycle, which has been in use for two centuries, and is a simple, affordable, reliable, clean and environmentally fit sustainable means of transportation.

National Egg Day on June 3 celebrates one of the most versatile ingredients in the kitchen. Eggs bind, thicken, leaven, and emulsify — making them indispensable in cooking and baking. The American Egg Board famously branded them 'The Incredible, Edible Egg' in 1976.

World Environment Day is the United Nations' principal vehicle for encouraging awareness and action for the protection of the environment. First held in 1974, it has grown to become the largest global platform for environmental public outreach.

slogans.en: Land restoration, desertification and drought resilience.

descriptions.en: Global Running Day on the first Wednesday of June is a worldwide celebration of running. It is a day to make a commitment to getting out for a run, however fast or slow, alone or with others.

slogans.en: One Day. One Run. One World.

descriptions.en: Denmark's Constitution Day (Grundlovsdag) on June 5 commemorates the signing of the Danish Constitution in 1849. The day is celebrated with political speeches and has traditionally been associated with women's rights movements.

World Donut Day on the first Friday of June was created in 1938 by the Salvation Army to honour volunteers who served donuts to soldiers during World War I. Today it is a sweet celebration enjoyed worldwide.
Sweden's National Day on June 6 celebrates the election of Gustav Vasa as King of Sweden in 1523 and the adoption of a new constitution in 1809. It became an official public holiday only in 2005.

slogans.en: För Sverige i Tiden! (For Sweden, with the Times!)

descriptions.en: Russian Language Day on June 6, established by the UN in 2010, celebrates one of the six official UN languages and honours Alexander Pushkin, born on this day in 1799, whose poetry and prose shaped modern Russian literature and the language spoken by hundreds of millions worldwide.

slogans.en: The Language of Pushkin Lives On.

descriptions.en: World Food Safety Day draws attention to the need to ensure that the food we eat is safe. Around 600 million people fall ill after eating contaminated food and 420,000 die every year as a result.

slogans.en: Food safety: prepare for the unexpected.

descriptions.en: World Chocolate Ice Cream Day is a deliciously fun celebration on June 7, inviting everyone to indulge in the timeless combination of chocolate and ice cream.

slogans.en: Life is Short, Eat Chocolate Ice Cream!

descriptions.en: World Ocean Day is an annual day of ocean celebration and action. The ocean covers more than 70% of our planet and produces at least 50% of the Earth's oxygen. It is home to most of Earth's biodiversity and is a main source of food and medicine for over 3 billion people.

slogans.en: One ocean, one climate, one future — together.

descriptions.en: Portugal Day on June 10 commemorates the death of Luís de Camões in 1580, Portugal's greatest poet and the author of 'Os Lusíadas'. The day also celebrates Portuguese culture and the nation's maritime heritage.

World Games Day encourages people of all ages to play games — board games, video games, outdoor games — celebrating play as a fundamental human activity that builds bonds, sharpens minds, and creates joy.
International Day of Play is observed to highlight the importance of play in children's development, well-being, and happiness. Play is a fundamental human right for children.

slogans.en: Play is the Language of Children

descriptions.en: National Making Life Beautiful Day is celebrated on June 11th to honor the power of beauty in all its forms—from art and creativity to kindness and meaningful connections. Founded by Apriori Beauty in 2015, this day encourages everyone to take intentional steps to enrich their surroundings, relationships, and inner selves.

The World Day Against Child Labour focuses global attention on the extent of child labour and the action needed to eliminate it. About 160 million children around the world are in child labour, with 79 million in hazardous work.

slogans.en: Social justice for all. End child labour.

descriptions.en: Russia Day on June 12 commemorates the Declaration of State Sovereignty of the Russian Federation in 1990. It was proclaimed as a national holiday in 1992.
Philippines Independence Day on June 12 commemorates the Declaration of Independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, when General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence in Kawit, Cavite.

World Pet Memorial Day, observed on the second Tuesday of June, is a global day to honour the memory of beloved pets who have passed. It's a time to celebrate the unconditional love they gave and the joy they brought into our lives.

slogans.en: Their love leaves paw prints on our hearts forever.

descriptions.en: World Blood Donor Day serves to raise awareness of the need for safe blood and blood products, and to thank voluntary, unpaid blood donors for their life-saving gifts of blood. Every 2 seconds someone needs blood.

slogans.en: Giving blood is an act of solidarity.

descriptions.en: World Juggling Day celebrates the art of juggling around the world. Jugglers of all skill levels perform and celebrate this timeless circus art.

slogans.en: Keep the Balls in the Air!

descriptions.en: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day on June 15 highlights the problem of physical, emotional, financial and social abuse suffered by older people around the world.

slogans.en: Lift Your Voice Against Elder Abuse.

descriptions.en: World Wind Day is observed every June 15 to raise awareness about wind energy, its power, and the possibilities it holds for reshaping our energy systems and decarbonizing economies.
Father's Day is a celebration honoring fathers and celebrating fatherhood, paternal bonds, and the influence of fathers in society. It is celebrated on the third Sunday in June in many countries.

World Sea Turtle Day honors these ancient creatures that have roamed the oceans for more than 100 million years. Today all seven species of sea turtles are threatened with extinction due to climate change, habitat loss, and plastic pollution.

Bloomsday is celebrated in Dublin and worldwide on June 16, the date on which James Joyce's novel Ulysses is set in 1904. Fans dress in Edwardian costume, read passages from the book, and follow Leopold Bloom's journey through Dublin.

slogans.en: Walking through Dublin with Leopold Bloom.

names.en: World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought

descriptions.en: This day provides a unique opportunity to remind everyone that land degradation neutrality is achievable through problem-solving, strong community involvement and cooperation at all levels. Droughts may affect over 75% of the world's population by 2050.

slogans.en: United for land. Our legacy. Our future.

descriptions.en: Iceland's National Day on June 17 marks the establishment of the Icelandic Republic in 1944, declaring independence from Denmark. The date was chosen to honour Jón Sigurdsson, leader of the Icelandic independence movement.

International Picnic Day celebrates the simple joy of sharing a meal outdoors with friends and family. Whether in a local park, a countryside meadow, or your own backyard, the day invites people to slow down, connect, and enjoy nature's dining room. Pack a basket, spread a blanket, and savor the al fresco life.

slogans.en: Pack a basket, share the joy.

descriptions.en: World Sickle Cell Day on June 19 raises awareness about sickle cell disease, one of the world's most common inherited blood disorders, and supports those living with it.
World Sauntering Day on June 19 encourages people to slow down, relax, and enjoy a leisurely stroll rather than rushing through life.

slogans.en: Slow Down and Smell the Roses

descriptions.en: Juneteenth commemorates the emancipation of enslaved African Americans in the United States. On June 19, 1865, Union soldiers arrived in Galveston, Texas, announcing that enslaved people were free — two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation.

World Refugee Day is an international day designated by the United Nations to honor refugees around the globe. It falls each year on June 20 and celebrates the strength, courage and perseverance of millions of refugees.
Argentina Flag Day (Día de la Bandera) on June 20 commemorates the death of Manuel Belgrano, the creator of the Argentine flag. It is an important national holiday.

slogans.en: Honoring the Blue and White — Viva Argentina!

descriptions.en: The International Day of Yoga aims to raise awareness worldwide of the many benefits of practicing yoga. Yoga is a physical, mental and spiritual practice that originated in ancient India and is now practiced by hundreds of millions worldwide.

names.en: World Music Day (Fête de la Musique)

descriptions.en: World Music Day, or Fête de la Musique, originated in France in 1982 and has since spread to hundreds of cities worldwide. On this day the summer solstice is celebrated with free outdoor music performances open to all.
World Giraffe Day on June 21 is an annual event created by the Giraffe Conservation Foundation to celebrate the longest day of the year by honouring the world's tallest animal.
Midsommar is a traditional Scandinavian celebration of the summer solstice, featuring maypole dancing, flower crowns, pickled herring, and outdoor festivities.

slogans.en: Dancing Around the Maypole — Welcome Summer!

descriptions.en: International Day of Yoga is celebrated annually on June 21 since 2015, following its declaration by the UN. Yoga is an ancient physical, mental, and spiritual practice that originated in India and is practiced by millions worldwide.
World Rainforest Day on June 22 celebrates the world's rainforests and raises awareness of the critical role they play in supporting life on Earth, from housing biodiversity to regulating climate.

National Kissing Day on June 22 celebrates the joy of kissing — romantic, friendly, or familial — and explores its history, health benefits, and cultural significance. A perfect day to show your loved ones some affection.

International Being You Day, founded in 2021 by Dr. Dain Heer, celebrates authenticity and the courage to be your true self. It's a day to embrace your uniqueness, let go of societal pressures, and let others show up as they are too.

Olympic Day was created to promote participation in sport around the globe, regardless of age, gender or athletic ability. The date refers to June 23, 1894, when the International Olympic Committee was founded.

St. John's Eve on June 23 is a mystical night celebrating the birth of John the Baptist — one of the few saints honoured on their birth rather than death. Communities across Spain, Portugal, Scandinavia, and Latin America mark the night with bonfires, herb gathering, and water rituals, blending centuries of Christian, folk, and solstice traditions into one spectacular celebration.

slogans.en: Jump the bonfire — let the midsummer magic begin.

descriptions.en: International Women in Engineering Day on June 23 celebrates the outstanding achievements of women engineers around the world and raises awareness of the exciting career opportunities open to girls in engineering. Launched in the UK in 2014 and given UNESCO patronage in 2016, the day shines a light on the brilliant women shaping our built world.

slogans.en: Women build the future — one breakthrough at a time.

descriptions.en: International Widows Day on June 23 is a United Nations observance dedicated to raising awareness of the rights, needs, and challenges facing the world's 258 million widows. Established by The Loomba Foundation in 2005 and recognised by the UN in 2010, June 23 was chosen because it marks the day the founder's mother became a widow in 1954.

Cat World Domination Day on June 24 is a playful celebration of cats' quiet control over their households — and possibly the world. Cats don't ask for power; they already have it. Give your feline overlord the worship they deserve.

slogans.en: Their silence speaks louder than barking ever could.

names.en: Take Your Dog to Work Day

descriptions.en: Take Your Dog to Work Day, founded in 1999 by Pet Sitters International, encourages workplaces to welcome employees' dogs for the day. It celebrates the human-animal bond, promotes pet adoption, and makes the office a whole lot happier.

slogans.en: Because who ever heard of working like a cat?

descriptions.en: Swim a Lap Day on June 24 encourages everyone to dive in and complete at least one lap of the pool. Swimming is a full-body, low-impact exercise that boosts heart health, relieves stress, and supports mobility for all ages — no competition required, just a great reason to get in the water.

slogans.en: One lap. All the benefits. Jump in.

names.en: International Day of Women in Diplomacy

descriptions.en: International Day of Women in Diplomacy, established by the UN General Assembly in 2022, highlights the vital role women play in international peace and foreign policy. From 1992–2019, women made up just 13% of peace negotiators — yet research shows peace agreements involving women are 35% more likely to last at least 15 years.

slogans.en: Women at the table build peace that lasts.

descriptions.en: World Fairy Day on June 24 — timed to the magic of Midsummer — celebrates the ancient folklore of fairies, sprites, and enchanted beings that have sparked human imagination across cultures for millennia. From Irish changelings and Scandinavian älvor to Shakespeare's Titania and Victorian fairy paintings, these winged beings of folklore bridge the mundane and the magical. The day is an invitation to read fairy tales, explore nature, craft tiny fairy doors, and let wonder take over.

slogans.en: Believe in a little magic today.

descriptions.en: International Day of the Seafarer, observed on June 25, honors the nearly 1.9 million merchant seafarers who keep global trade moving — carrying roughly 80% of world merchandise by sea. Established by the International Maritime Organization (IMO) in 2010 and first observed in 2011, the day shines a light on seafarers' rights, mental health, and the often invisible sacrifices of those who spend months away from family on the open ocean.

slogans.en: The world moves because they do.

descriptions.en: Social Justice Sunday is observed across Australia, anchored in a tradition begun by Australian Catholic bishops in 1940 to address pressing social, economic, and ecological concerns. Each year the bishops release a statement focusing on a different theme — poverty, inequality, environmental care — calling on the Catholic community and beyond to reflect, act, and engage. The day invites personal action plans, community panels, food drives, letter-writing to representatives, social-justice movie nights, and volunteering to make solidarity and compassionate action feel tangible.

slogans.en: Reflect, act, and stand for fairness.

descriptions.en: The Philippines' National Heroes Day falls on the last Monday in August, marking the 1896 Cry of Pugad Lawin that launched the Philippine Revolution against the Spanish Empire. The day honours figures like Andres Bonifacio, who founded the Katipunan, and Apolinario Mabini, the brilliant paralysed strategist known as the Sublime Paralytic, alongside every Filipino who served and sacrificed for the nation. Observed since 1931 with parades, wreath-layings, fireworks, and quiet reflection, the modern celebration was moved to its long-weekend date in 2007. Other countries honour their own heroes on different dates — Zimbabwe remembers its Liberation War heroes on the second Monday of August, Indonesia on 10 November, the Cayman Islands on the fourth Monday in January.

The Late Summer Bank Holiday (also called the August Bank Holiday) falls on the last Monday in August in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, marking the third three-day weekend British workers earn each summer. Introduced by the Bank Holidays Act of 1871 to improve conditions for industrial workers, it was moved to the last Monday of August in 1971's Banking and Financial Dealings Act so families could enjoy a long weekend. The day sees millions take short holidays, fire up barbecues for one of the last outdoor meals of the season, head to Brighton or Blackpool, and crowd the Notting Hill Carnival.

slogans.en: One last long weekend. Make it count.

descriptions.en: National Day of Joy, held on the last Wednesday of June, encourages people to find and share happiness in everyday moments. Created in 2019 by Comfort Keepers — an in-home senior care organization — the day grew from the observation that small moments of happiness often bring the biggest smiles. Joy isn't reserved for weekends or special occasions: it's a skill that can be practiced, noticed, and shared every single day.

slogans.en: Joy is a skill — practice it today.

descriptions.en: The International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking, observed on June 26, is a UN day to raise awareness of the major challenge that illicit drugs represent and strengthen global action and cooperation to combat the drug problem.

slogans.en: People First: Stop Stigma and Discrimination.

descriptions.en: National Beauticians Day on June 26 honors cosmetologists and beauty professionals worldwide — from hairstylists and colorists to estheticians, nail technicians, and makeup artists. These skilled professionals blend artistry with technical expertise, helping clients feel confident and polished every day. The beauty industry traces its professional roots to ancient Egypt and Imperial Rome, and became a regulated licensed profession in the early 20th century, with pioneers like Madam C.J. Walker opening beauty colleges for Black women as early as 1908.

slogans.en: Beauty is their craft. Confidence is their gift.

descriptions.en: Cancer Wellness Awareness Day on June 26 promotes holistic support for people affected by cancer — going beyond medical treatment to embrace movement, nutrition, emotional wellbeing, and community connection. Founded in 2019 by the West Island Cancer Wellness Centre in Quebec, the day affirms that wellness support is not a luxury but a meaningful part of comprehensive cancer care. Exercise reduces cancer-related fatigue, Mediterranean-style diets are linked to a 16% reduction in cancer mortality, and peer support fosters a greater sense of control and meaning.

slogans.en: Wellness is not a luxury — it's part of the cure.

descriptions.en: National Chocolate Pudding Day on June 26 celebrates one of America's most beloved comfort desserts. Chocolate pudding's story stretches from 18th-century baked custards to Alfred Bird's egg-free custard powder in 1837 and the first boxed pudding mix from My-T-Fine in 1918. Today it comes in endless forms — classic milk chocolate, dark, white, mint — topped with whipped cream, caramel, or sprinkles. Creamy, nostalgic, and endlessly customizable.

Dream Big Day, held on the last Friday of June, inspires children to explore their interests, break down barriers, and imagine ambitious futures. Organized by Careermap and sponsored by Pearson, Barclays, and Lifeskills, the day connects UK employers with primary schools to bring real-world career education to young learners. Research shows children's career aspirations narrow dramatically by age seven — so introducing diverse possibilities early makes a lasting difference.

slogans.en: Every big life starts with a big dream.

descriptions.en: National SAFER Workplace Day, held on the last Friday of June, encourages workers across all industries to Stop, Assess, Formulate, Execute, and Review safety in their daily tasks. Founded in 2023 by tec.nicum (part of the Schmersal Group), the day began with a focus on machine safety before expanding to cover all workplaces — offices, factories, warehouses. It emphasizes real actions over just talk: hazard discussions, safety reviews, and proactive risk identification.

slogans.en: Safety starts with a single smart step.

descriptions.en: Micro, Small and Medium-sized Enterprises Day, observed on June 27, recognizes the critical contribution of MSMEs to sustainable development and the global economy. MSMEs represent about 90% of all businesses worldwide.

names.en: Industrial Workers of the World Day

descriptions.en: Industrial Workers of the World Day on June 27 marks the founding of the IWW in Chicago in 1905 — the union that pioneered 'industrial unionism,' organizing all workers across an entire industry rather than dividing them by trade. Famous for the rallying cry 'an injury to one is an injury to all,' the IWW shaped modern labor through landmark struggles like the 1912 Lawrence Textile Strike. The day honors both that history and the often-invisible industrial work that keeps society running today.

slogans.en: An injury to one is an injury to all.

descriptions.en: Global Smurf Day fills the streets with blue faces, white hats, and wide smiles. Established in 2011 by Sony Pictures Animation to celebrate the birthday of Peyo — the Belgian artist who created the little blue characters in 1958 — the inaugural event earned a Guinness World Record for the largest gathering of people dressed as Smurfs. Held on the Saturday closest to June 25, the day celebrates imagination, kindness, and teamwork through costumes, parties, and comic marathons.

UK Armed Forces Day, held on the last Saturday of June, celebrates the entire British military community — serving personnel, reservists, veterans, cadets, and military families. It began in 2006 as Veterans' Day and was renamed and expanded in 2009 to honour the armed forces as an active part of national life. Through parades, family events, and community open houses, the day helps bridge the gap that can form between military and civilian life.

slogans.en: Show your support for our Armed Forces.

descriptions.en: Happy Heart Hugs Day on June 28 is dedicated to sending love and virtual hugs to the people who fill your heart with happiness but live too far away for a real embrace. Reach out with a message, a call, or a heartfelt note.

slogans.en: Distance can't stop a heart full of love.

descriptions.en: The International Day of the Tropics, celebrated on June 29, raises awareness of the unique challenges faced by tropical regions and highlights the extraordinary diversity and opportunities they represent.

Social Media Day was launched by Mashable in 2010 to recognize social media's impact on global communication. It celebrates how social platforms have revolutionized the way we connect, share, and engage with the world.
Canada Day on July 1 marks the anniversary of Confederation in 1867, when the British North America Act united Canada, Nova Scotia, and New Brunswick into a single Dominion of Canada.

slogans.en: O Canada! True North Strong and Free.

descriptions.en: International Reggae Day (July 1) celebrates reggae music originating from Jamaica in the 1960s. Reggae is recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage. Its messages of peace, love, and social justice resonate worldwide.

On July 1, 1926, Turkey's Cabotage Law (No. 815) came into effect, granting Turkish citizens the exclusive right to maritime trade and navigation in Turkish territorial waters — ending decades of foreign dominance over Turkey's seas.

World UFO Day on July 2 marks the 1947 Roswell incident, a day to raise awareness about extraterrestrial life and UFOs, and to encourage people to look up at the skies and wonder about what else might be out there.

slogans.en: Look Up. The Truth is Out There.

descriptions.en: The Palio di Siena is a historic horse race held twice a year (July 2 and August 16) in Siena, Italy, around the Piazza del Campo. Ten of Siena's seventeen contrade (districts) compete in this medieval tradition dating back to the 13th century.

slogans.en: Siena's heartbeat — the thunder of hooves.

descriptions.en: International Plastic Bag Free Day urges people around the world to ditch single-use plastic bags and opt for reusable alternatives. Over 5 trillion plastic bags are used each year, polluting oceans and harming wildlife.

slogans.en: Refuse the bag. Rescue the planet.

descriptions.en: The Fourth of July is the United States' Independence Day, celebrating the adoption of the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776. It is marked with fireworks, parades, barbecues, concerts, and family gatherings.

slogans.en: Land of the free, home of the brave.

descriptions.en: Pet Remembrance Day on July 5 honours the beloved animals we've lost and the unforgettable bond we shared with them. A day to look back on cherished memories and celebrate the pawprint they left on our hearts forever.

slogans.en: Their pawprints stay on our hearts forever.

descriptions.en: World Chocolate Day, sometimes referred to as International Chocolate Day, is an annual celebration of chocolate. The date is believed to celebrate the introduction of chocolate to Europe in 1550.
Argentina Independence Day on July 9 marks the declaration of independence in 1816 from Spanish rule. The country celebrates with patriotic events, concerts, and traditional foods.

World Population Day is an annual event observed every July 11 to raise awareness about global population issues. The world's population reached 5 billion on July 11, 1987. Today, we are over 8 billion people.

Malala Day is the United Nations' official day in honor of Malala Yousafzai. It is a day for people to raise their voices for girls' education worldwide. Malala was the youngest person ever to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

slogans.en: One child, one teacher, one book, one pen can change the world.

descriptions.en: World Day of Rock Music is celebrated on July 13 to commemorate the legendary Live Aid concert of 1985, which raised funds for famine relief in Ethiopia. It is a day to celebrate rock music and its cultural impact.

slogans.en: Rock On! Music Unites the World.

descriptions.en: Bastille Day is the French National Day, celebrated on 14 July each year. In France it is called La Fête Nationale. It commemorates the Storming of the Bastille on July 14, 1789, which was a turning point in the French Revolution.

World Chimpanzee Day celebrates our closest living relatives, with whom we share 98.7% of our DNA. It raises awareness of the threats facing chimpanzees including habitat destruction, disease, and illegal bushmeat trade.

slogans.en: Our closest cousins need our help.

descriptions.en: Democracy and National Unity Day commemorates the defeat of the coup attempt on the night of July 15–16, 2016. Citizens took to the streets in response to President Erdoğan's call, and the attempt was repelled by the early hours of July 16. The day became a public holiday in 2017 to honour those who lost their lives defending democracy and to remember the night Turkey resisted a military takeover.

slogans.en: Democracy is the voice of the people.

descriptions.en: World Snake Day on July 16 is dedicated to raising awareness of the many different species of snakes in the world, celebrating their role in ecology, and reducing fear.

World Emoji Day is an annual event on July 17 celebrating emoji. The date was chosen because it is the date displayed on the Calendar emoji in iOS. With over 3,600 emoji currently in the Unicode Standard, emojis have become a universal language.

Nelson Mandela International Day is an annual international day in honour of Nelson Mandela, celebrated each year on his birthday, July 18. The idea is to inspire individuals to take action to help change the world for the better by dedicating 67 minutes of time to public service.

World Ice Cream Day falls on the third Sunday of July. It was created by US President Ronald Reagan in 1984 who designated July as National Ice Cream Month. Ice cream is enjoyed in over 100 countries worldwide.

slogans.en: Life is Short, Eat More Ice Cream.

descriptions.en: World Chess Day on July 20 marks the day the International Chess Federation (FIDE) was founded in 1924. Chess is one of the oldest and most universal strategy games and is played in virtually every country.

Colombia's Independence Day on July 20 commemorates the uprising of 1810 that began the process of independence from Spain. The Cry of Independence (Grito de Independencia) is celebrated throughout the country.

International Chess Day is observed on July 20, the day FIDE was founded in Paris in 1924. Chess is one of the oldest and most popular strategy games in the world, played by over 600 million people across all cultures.

Space Exploration Day (July 20) commemorates the date in 1969 when Neil Armstrong became the first human to walk on the Moon. It celebrates the spirit of human exploration, scientific discovery, and the quest to reach beyond our planet.

slogans.en: One small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.

descriptions.en: Belgium's National Day on July 21 celebrates the inauguration of King Leopold I in 1831, who became the first King of the Belgians following independence from the Netherlands.

slogans.en: Eendracht maakt macht — Unity is Strength.

descriptions.en: World Brain Day is organized by the World Federation of Neurology to raise awareness and promote brain health. Each year focuses on a specific neurological condition to advance prevention and treatment worldwide.

Egypt's Revolution Day on July 23 commemorates the Egyptian Revolution of 1952 when the Free Officers Movement led by Muhammad Naguib and Gamal Abdel Nasser overthrew King Farouk and ended British influence.
World Whale and Dolphin Day on July 23 celebrates these magnificent marine mammals and raises awareness about protecting them and their ocean habitats.

International Self Care Day on July 24 emphasizes that the benefits of self-care are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Good self-care reduces chronic disease, improves mental health, and is the foundation of sustainable well-being.

slogans.en: Self care is not selfish — it's essential.
