descriptions.en: World Drowning Prevention Day was proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in 2021. Around 295,000 people drown every year — making it one of the leading causes of unintentional injury death worldwide. Drowning is almost entirely preventable.

names.en: International Day for the Conservation of the Mangrove Ecosystem

descriptions.en: This day raises awareness of the importance of mangrove ecosystems as 'a unique, special and vulnerable ecosystem.' Mangroves cover a little over 150,000 km² of land surface globally and are a vital barrier protecting coastal communities from storm surges.

World Hepatitis Day is observed every July 28 to raise global awareness about hepatitis — a group of infectious diseases known as Hepatitis A, B, C, D, and E. Around 354 million people globally live with hepatitis B or C.
World Swimming Day on July 28 celebrates the sport of swimming and encourages people of all ages to take to the water. Swimming is one of the most complete forms of exercise and a vital life skill.
Peru's Independence Day on July 28 commemorates General José de San Martín's proclamation of independence from Spain in 1821. The celebration continues on July 29 as Armed Forces Day.
World Nature Conservation Day on July 28 acknowledges that a healthy environment is the foundation for a stable and productive society, and to protect the nature we love.

slogans.en: Conserve Nature for a Better Tomorrow

descriptions.en: International Tiger Day, also known as Global Tiger Day, is observed annually to raise awareness for tiger conservation. Tigers are listed as Endangered by the IUCN Red List. There are fewer than 4,000 wild tigers remaining on Earth.

slogans.en: Saving tigers is saving our planet.

descriptions.en: Global Tiger Day (International Tiger Day) is celebrated on July 29 to raise awareness of tiger conservation and to protect tiger habitats worldwide.

The International Day of Friendship was proclaimed in 2011 by the UN General Assembly with the idea that friendship between peoples, countries, cultures and individuals can inspire peace efforts and build bridges between communities.

slogans.en: Sharing the human spirit through friendship.

descriptions.en: The World Day Against Trafficking in Persons, observed on July 30, raises awareness about the situation of victims of human trafficking and for the promotion and protection of their rights.

slogans.en: Act to Protect. Act to Support.

descriptions.en: Morocco's Throne Day on July 30 celebrates the accession of King Mohammed VI to the throne in 1999. It is one of Morocco's most important national holidays, marked by royal speeches, fireworks, and patriotic events.

slogans.en: Long Live His Majesty the King!

descriptions.en: World Avocado Day on July 31 celebrates the green superfood that has conquered the world. From guacamole to avocado toast, the avocado has become one of the most popular and versatile foods.

World Ranger Day commemorates rangers killed or injured in the line of duty and celebrates their contribution to protecting the world's natural and cultural heritage. Rangers are the frontline defenders of wildlife.

Swiss National Day (Bundesfeiertag) is celebrated on August 1 and commemorates the creation of the Swiss Confederation in 1291. The date recalls the Federal Charter of 1291, one of the founding documents of Switzerland.

International Beer Day on the first Friday of August is a global celebration of beer, bringing together friends and strangers to enjoy a cold pint. It is a day to toast to brewers and bartenders worldwide.

World Wide Web Day celebrates the birthday of the World Wide Web, invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989. The web has transformed every aspect of human society and become an indispensable tool for communication, commerce, and knowledge sharing.
National Watermelon Day on August 3 celebrates one of summer's most beloved fruits. Cool, sweet, and refreshing, watermelon is enjoyed globally during hot summer days.

International Cat Day on August 8 celebrates one of humanity's oldest and most beloved companions. It was created in 2002 by the International Fund for Animal Welfare to recognise cats and learn how to protect them.
World Cat Day on August 8 celebrates cats and raises awareness of their welfare. Cat lovers worldwide honor their feline companions with special attention and treats.

slogans.en: Because Every Day Should Be Cat Day

names.en: International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples

descriptions.en: The International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples is observed on August 9 each year to raise awareness and protect the rights of the world's indigenous population. This event also recognizes the achievements and contributions of indigenous people.

slogans.en: Indigenous peoples and a new social contract.

descriptions.en: International Book Lovers Day on August 9 celebrates the joy of reading and encourages people to pick up a book. It is a day to share reading lists, visit libraries, and celebrate the worlds found in the pages of a good book.

slogans.en: Open a Book, Open Your Mind.

descriptions.en: Singapore's National Day on August 9 commemorates the republic's separation from Malaysia and declaration of independence in 1965. It is celebrated with a grand parade and spectacular fireworks at Marina Bay.
National S'mores Day on August 10 celebrates the classic campfire treat of marshmallow and chocolate sandwiched between graham crackers. It is a beloved symbol of outdoor adventures and summer fun.

World Lion Day raises awareness about the plight of lions, whose numbers have dropped by over 40% in the past three decades. These iconic big cats now occupy only 8% of their historical range and face threats from habitat loss and human conflict.

slogans.en: Roar for the king of the savanna.

descriptions.en: National Classic Movie Day on August 10 celebrates the timeless films that shaped the art of cinema. From golden-age Hollywood epics to beloved mid-century comedies and dramas, this day is a perfect excuse to revisit a cinematic masterpiece.
International Youth Day is an awareness day designated by the United Nations. The purpose of the day is to draw attention to a given set of cultural and legal issues surrounding youth.

slogans.en: Green skills for youth: towards a sustainable world.

descriptions.en: World Elephant Day was launched on August 12, 2012, to bring attention to the urgent plight of Asian and African elephants. It calls on people worldwide to help protect these magnificent animals from threats like poaching and habitat loss.
International Left-Handers Day on August 13 celebrates the uniqueness and diversity of left-handers. It raises awareness of the everyday challenges faced by left-handers in a right-hand-biased world.

Obon is a Japanese Buddhist tradition held each August 13–15 to honor the spirits of ancestors. Families return home, clean grave sites, and light lanterns to guide spirits back. The festival features Bon Odori folk dances, floating paper lanterns on rivers, and a profound sense of togetherness across generations.

Pakistan Independence Day on August 14 marks the creation of Pakistan as an independent nation in 1947, carved out of British India following the partition. The day is celebrated with flag-hoisting ceremonies and patriotic events.

India's Independence Day is celebrated on August 15 each year to commemorate India's independence from British rule on August 15, 1947. The day is a national holiday in India, marked with flag-hoisting ceremonies, parades, and cultural events.
Korea Liberation Day on August 15 (Gwangbokjeol) commemorates the liberation of Korea from Japanese occupation in 1945. In South Korea it also marks the establishment of the South Korean government.

slogans.en: Gwangbokjeol: Light Returns to the Nation.

descriptions.en: Assumption Day celebrates the bodily assumption of the Virgin Mary into heaven. It is a public holiday in Bavaria and Saarland, observed with processions and church services.

Indonesia's Independence Day on August 17 commemorates the Proclamation of Indonesian Independence on 17 August 1945 by Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta. It is celebrated with flag-raising ceremonies and traditional games.

World Humanitarian Day is held annually on August 19 to pay tribute to aid workers who risk or lose their lives in humanitarian service and to rally support for people affected by crises around the world.
World Photography Day, celebrated on August 19, is a global celebration of photography art, craft, science, and history, dating back to the invention of the daguerreotype in 1837.

slogans.en: A Photo Captures a Moment Forever

descriptions.en: World Mosquito Day on August 20 commemorates Sir Ronald Ross's 1897 discovery that female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria between humans.

Ukraine's Independence Day on August 24 marks the Act of Independence of Ukraine declared in 1991 following the dissolution of the Soviet Union. It is celebrated with parades and cultural events in Kyiv.

International Dog Day on August 26 celebrates the love of dogs and honors all breeds, from the purebred to the mixed-breed shelter dog. It was founded by Animal Welfare Advocate Colleen Paige in 2004.

slogans.en: Every Dog Deserves a Loving Home.

descriptions.en: The International Day Against Nuclear Tests was declared by the UN General Assembly to commemorate the closure of the Semipalatinsk Test Site in Kazakhstan and to foster global nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation.

slogans.en: For a world free of nuclear tests.

descriptions.en: Victory Day (Zafer Bayramı) on August 30 commemorates the decisive Battle of Dumlupınar in 1922, the final battle of the Turkish War of Independence which established the modern Turkish state.

International Whale Shark Day celebrates the world's largest fish and raises awareness about their threatened status. These gentle giants can reach 12 meters in length yet are endangered due to boat strikes, fishing, and habitat degradation.

slogans.en: The gentle giant needs a gentle hand.

descriptions.en: Frankenstein Day marks Mary Shelley's 1818 novel, the book that invented modern science fiction. Written when she was just 19, it tells the story of Victor Frankenstein and the Creature he stitches together from cadavers and jolts to life with lightning — a haunting meditation on ambition, creation, isolation, and what it means to be human. Readers, watchers, and writers celebrate the novel by revisiting the book, watching one of dozens of film adaptations, dressing up, exploring Frankenstein-themed video games, or simply talking about how a teenager gave us an idea that has haunted every scientific breakthrough since.

slogans.en: One spark, one monster, one legend.

descriptions.en: Malaysia's National Day (Hari Merdeka) on August 31 commemorates the independence of Malaya from British rule on August 31, 1957. The day is celebrated with colorful parades and patriotic events in Kuala Lumpur.

International Overdose Awareness Day is the world's largest annual campaign to end overdose, remember without stigma those who have died and acknowledge the grief of the family and friends left behind.
World Alzheimer's Month is the international campaign every September to raise awareness and challenge the stigma surrounding dementia and Alzheimer's disease.
Vietnam National Day on September 2 commemorates Ho Chi Minh's Declaration of Independence in 1945, establishing the Democratic Republic of Vietnam after the end of World War II.

slogans.en: Độc lập – Tự do – Hạnh phúc (Independence – Freedom – Happiness)

descriptions.en: World Coconut Day on September 2 promotes the importance of the coconut palm and its products for the economic well-being of coconut-growing communities worldwide.
Vietnam National Day on September 2 marks the declaration of independence by Ho Chi Minh in 1945, establishing the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.

slogans.en: Độc lập — Tự do — Hạnh phúc!

descriptions.en: The International Day of Charity is observed to raise awareness and provide a common platform for charity-related activities all over the world. September 5 is the anniversary of the death of Mother Teresa in 1997.
Brazil Independence Day on September 7 marks the day in 1822 when Prince Pedro I declared Brazil's independence from Portugal by shouting the famous Grito do Ipiranga ('Cry from Ipiranga').

International Literacy Day was proclaimed by UNESCO in 1966. It reminds the public of the importance of literacy as a matter of dignity and human rights, and to advance the literacy agenda towards a more literate and sustainable society. Around 773 million adults worldwide lack basic literacy skills.

slogans.en: Promoting literacy for a world in transition: building the foundation for sustainable and peaceful societies.

descriptions.en: National Pet Memorial Day, observed on the second Sunday of September in the US, is a day to remember and celebrate the lives of pets who have passed. Light a candle, visit a favourite spot, or share a memory to keep their spirit alive.

slogans.en: Gone but never forgotten — always in our hearts.

descriptions.en: World Suicide Prevention Day on September 10 is organised by the International Association for Suicide Prevention. It is dedicated to providing worldwide commitment and action to prevent suicides.

International Programmers' Day is celebrated on the 256th day of the year (September 13 in common years). 256 was chosen because it is the number of distinct values that can be represented with a single byte.

slogans.en: There are 10 types of people in the world.

descriptions.en: Roald Dahl Day celebrates the birthday of Roald Dahl (September 13, 1916), author of beloved children's classics including Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, Matilda, and The BFG. His imagination continues to enchant millions worldwide.

slogans.en: A little nonsense now and then is relished by the wisest men.

descriptions.en: Bald is Beautiful Day on September 13 celebrates the confidence and pride of bald people everywhere. It challenges beauty norms and champions the idea that hairlessness is not a flaw — it's a feature.

slogans.en: No hair, no problem — shine on!

descriptions.en: World First Aid Day is held on the second Saturday of September each year to promote first aid awareness and teach basic first aid skills to more people.

slogans.en: Know First Aid, Save a Life

descriptions.en: The International Day of Democracy provides an opportunity to review the state of democracy in the world. Democracy is as much a process as a goal, and only with the full participation of and support by the international community can the ideal of democracy be made into a reality.

Greenpeace Day on September 15 marks the 1971 voyage that gave the movement its name, when a small crew sailed a chartered fishing boat toward Amchitka in Alaska to bear witness against nuclear testing. They were turned back, but the protest carried, and the test site closed the following year.
World Ozone Day commemorates the date in 1987 when the Montreal Protocol was signed to protect the ozone layer. The ozone layer shields the Earth from harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun.

slogans.en: Montreal Protocol: fixing the ozone layer and reducing climate change.

descriptions.en: Mexican Independence Day celebrates the beginning of Mexico's war of independence from Spain in 1810. The day is known for the Grito de Independencia (Cry of Independence), fireworks, parades, and festive celebrations.

The Swiss Federal Fast (Eidgenössischer Dank-, Buss- und Bettag) falls on the third Sunday of September. It is one of the few federal public holidays in Switzerland, observed as a day of prayer, gratitude, and fasting.

slogans.en: One for All, All for One.

descriptions.en: World Patient Safety Day was established by the WHO to increase global understanding of patient safety and reduce patient harm. It calls for solidarity and collective action to improve safety in healthcare settings worldwide.

World Manta Day celebrates and raises awareness about manta rays, some of the ocean's most majestic creatures. Manta rays are threatened by targeted fishing and bycatch, and are listed as vulnerable by the IUCN.

slogans.en: Protect the gentle giants of the sea.

descriptions.en: Chile's Independence Day on September 18 celebrates the First National Government Junta of 1810. Known as Fiestas Patrias, the celebration includes traditional dances like cueca, typical food, and patriotic events.

World Bamboo Day raises awareness about the benefits of bamboo. The fastest-growing plant on Earth, bamboo sequesters carbon, prevents soil erosion, and provides sustainable materials as an alternative to plastic and deforestation-linked timber.
International Equal Pay Day represents the ongoing effort towards the achievement of equal pay for work of equal value. Women globally still earn approximately 20% less than men for comparable work.

slogans.en: Equal pay for equal work — always.

names.en: International Talk Like a Pirate Day

descriptions.en: International Talk Like a Pirate Day is a parodic holiday created in 1995 by John Baur and Mark Summers. On this day, people are encouraged to talk in the stereotypical language of pirates — 'Ahoy!', 'Shiver me timbers!', and 'Arr!'
World Cleanup Day is a global civic movement, uniting people around the world in the world's biggest positive civic action — cleaning up the world.

The International Day of Peace provides an opportunity for all humanity to commit to peace above all differences and to contribute to building a culture of peace. The day is observed by 24 hours of non-violence and cease-fire.

slogans.en: Actions for peace: our ambition for the #GlobalGoals.

descriptions.en: World Alzheimer's Day on September 21 is an international campaign by Alzheimer's Disease International to raise awareness and challenge the stigma that surrounds dementia.
Software Freedom Day is an annual worldwide celebration of Free Software. The goal is to educate the worldwide public about the benefits of using high quality free and open-source software.

slogans.en: Free Software for a Free World

descriptions.en: Oktoberfest is the world's largest beer festival held annually in Munich, Germany. Millions of visitors from around the world attend to enjoy Bavarian culture, beer, and food.

slogans.en: O'zapft is! — Let the Festivities Begin!

descriptions.en: World Rhino Day was established in 2010 and is now celebrated worldwide to raise awareness about the five species of rhino — all of which are threatened with extinction due to poaching and habitat loss.

slogans.en: Five rhino species, five reasons to act.

descriptions.en: Hobbit Day on September 22 celebrates the birthday of Bilbo and Frodo Baggins, beloved characters from J. R. R. Tolkien's The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings.

slogans.en: In a hole in the ground, there lived a hobbit.

descriptions.en: International Day of Sign Languages was established to raise awareness of the importance of sign language as a means of realizing the human rights of deaf people. There are over 300 different sign languages used worldwide.

slogans.en: Sign language — a language of inclusion.

descriptions.en: Celebrate Bisexuality Day, also known as Bisexual Pride Day or Bi Visibility Day, is observed on September 23 to acknowledge and celebrate bisexual people, history, community, and culture.

Heritage Day in South Africa on September 24 celebrates the cultural heritage, diversity, and history of South Africa. Fondly known as 'Braai Day', it is a time for South Africans to gather around the fire and celebrate their rainbow nation.
World Gorilla Day on September 24 celebrates gorillas and raises awareness for their protection. Gorillas are critically endangered and need conservation efforts.

World Pharmacists' Day is celebrated every year on September 25 — the anniversary of the founding of the International Pharmaceutical Federation (FIP) in 1912. Established by FIP in 2009, the day highlights the vital role pharmacists play in improving health worldwide, promoting safe medication use, and advancing pharmaceutical science. Each year focuses on a specific theme set by FIP.

World Environmental Health Day on September 26 highlights the role that the natural environment plays in human health and well-being. It promotes the importance of clean air, safe water, and healthy ecosystems for public health.

National Pancake Day on September 26 celebrates America's love for the fluffy stacks that define weekend mornings. From classic buttermilk to blueberry and banana, pancakes are a canvas for creativity and a warm comfort food shared across generations. Stack 'em high and pour on the syrup!
World Tourism Day on September 27 was established by the World Tourism Organization in 1980 to foster awareness of the importance of tourism and its social, cultural, political and economic values.

National Chocolate Milk Day on September 27 celebrates the childhood classic that turns a plain glass of milk into a treat. Cocoa, a little sweetness and cold milk — a combination that doubles as a favorite recovery drink after a hard workout.
World Rabies Day on September 28 raises awareness about rabies prevention and the progress we have made globally to defeat this disease.

World Heart Day was created to inform people around the globe that heart disease and stroke are the world's leading causes of death, claiming 18.6 million lives each year. The day encourages people to make heart-healthy choices.

International Translation Day is celebrated on September 30, the Feast Day of St. Jerome, patron saint of translators. It is an opportunity to show solidarity within the translation community and to promote the translation profession.

International Podcast Day celebrates podcasting as a transformative medium for storytelling, education, and connection. There are now over 3 million active podcasts globally, making audio content more accessible than ever.

The International Day of Older Persons is observed on October 1. It was established by the United Nations in 1990. The day celebrates the contributions of older people and raises awareness of the opportunities and challenges of ageing in today's world.

International Coffee Day is a celebration of the beloved beverage. It is used to promote and celebrate coffee as a beverage, with events occurring in cafes and coffee shops around the world. More than 2 billion cups of coffee are consumed every day worldwide.

China National Day is celebrated on October 1 to mark the anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949. It is the most important national holiday in China, featuring a week-long 'Golden Week' holiday.

slogans.en: Long live the People's Republic of China!

descriptions.en: Nigeria's Independence Day on October 1 commemorates the country's independence from British colonial rule in 1960. Nigeria, Africa's most populous nation, celebrates with parades, cultural events, and national pride.

slogans.en: Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress.

descriptions.en: World Vegetarian Day on October 1 is an annual celebration of vegetarianism. It promotes the joy and compassion of vegetarian living and advocates for a plant-based diet.
The International Day of Non-Violence is observed on 2 October, the birthday of Mahatma Gandhi, leader of the Indian independence movement and pioneer of the philosophy and strategy of non-violence.

slogans.en: Be the change you wish to see in the world.

descriptions.en: German Unity Day is the national day of Germany and celebrates the anniversary of German reunification on October 3, 1990. It is the only German national public holiday that is determined by a real historical event.
World Animal Day is an international day of action for animal rights and welfare. The mission is to raise the status of animals in order to improve welfare standards around the globe.

slogans.en: Creating a world where animals are always recognized as sentient beings.

descriptions.en: World Smile Day is held on the first Friday of October. Harvey Ball, the commercial artist who designed the smiley face in 1963, started World Smile Day in 1999 with the motto: 'Do an act of kindness. Help one person smile.'

slogans.en: Do an Act of Kindness. Help One Person Smile.

names.en: Feast of St. Francis of Assisi

descriptions.en: The Feast of St. Francis of Assisi (October 4) honors the patron saint of animals, the environment, and Italy. Many churches hold Blessing of the Animals ceremonies. Francis is celebrated for his love of nature and creatures.

slogans.en: All creatures great and small — blessed.

descriptions.en: World Teachers Day, held on October 5, celebrates the teaching profession worldwide. It commemorates the signing in 1966 of the ILO/UNESCO Recommendation concerning the Status of Teachers.

slogans.en: Teachers at the Heart of Education Recovery.

descriptions.en: World Cerebral Palsy Day is a global movement of people with cerebral palsy and their families, fighting for a world where people with CP have the same rights, access, and opportunities as anyone else.
World Habitat Day is observed on the first Monday of October. It reflects on the state of our towns and cities and the right of all to adequate shelter.

World Architecture Day is observed on the first Monday of October. It was established by the International Union of Architects to celebrate architecture's role in shaping the built environment and improving human lives.

World Post Day is celebrated each year on October 9 to mark the anniversary of the establishment of the Universal Postal Union in 1874 in Bern, Switzerland. It is used to raise awareness of the postal sector's role in everyday life.

slogans.en: Post for planet: Together for a sustainable future.

descriptions.en: Hangul Day (Hangul Proclamation Day) is a national holiday in South Korea on October 9, commemorating the creation and proclamation of Hangul, the Korean alphabet.

slogans.en: Celebrating the Beauty of the Korean Script

descriptions.en: Global Beatles Day on June 25 commemorates the 1967 broadcast of 'All You Need Is Love' — the first-ever live international satellite television event, watched by 400 million people worldwide. Established in 2009 by fan Faith Cohen as a love letter to the band, the day celebrates The Beatles' music, message of peace, and their unmatched cultural legacy. With over 600 million albums sold and 20 Billboard #1 hits, they remain the best-selling music artists in history.
World Mental Health Day on October 10 is an international day for global mental health education, awareness, and advocacy against social stigma.

slogans.en: Mental Health is a Universal Human Right

names.en: International Day of the Girl Child

descriptions.en: International Day of the Girl Child focuses attention on the need to address the challenges girls face and to promote girls' empowerment and the fulfilment of their human rights. Girls everywhere face discrimination and disadvantage from the moment they are born.

slogans.en: Our time is now — our rights, our future.

descriptions.en: World Egg Day is celebrated on the second Friday of October each year to promote the benefits of eggs as a food source that is healthy, nutritious, and accessible to all.

National Coming Out Day (NCOD) is observed on October 11 to support LGBT+ individuals in the process of coming out. Founded in 1988, it celebrates LGBTQ+ identity and communities and promotes a safe world for all people.

slogans.en: Be yourself. Everyone else is taken.

descriptions.en: World Sight Day, observed on the second Thursday of October, is an annual day of awareness to focus global attention on blindness and vision impairment.
Spain's National Day on October 12 commemorates the arrival of Christopher Columbus in the Americas in 1492. It also celebrates the Hispanic heritage that links Spain with Latin American countries.

Bald and Free Day on October 14 takes it a step further — it's a day to fully embrace, celebrate, and flaunt baldness without reservation. Whether naturally bald or shaved by choice, today is your day.

slogans.en: Free your head, free your mind.

descriptions.en: Global Handwashing Day on October 15 is a global advocacy day dedicated to increasing awareness and understanding about the importance of handwashing with soap as an easy, effective, and affordable way to prevent diseases.

slogans.en: Clean Hands Are a Human Right.

descriptions.en: World Food Day is celebrated every year around the world on October 16 in honor of the date of the founding of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations in 1945. It is observed to raise awareness of the need to fight hunger and ensure food security.

slogans.en: Water is life, water is food. Leave no one behind.

descriptions.en: World Bread Day on October 16 celebrates one of humanity's oldest foods. Observed by bakers and food enthusiasts around the world, it encourages people to bake and appreciate fresh bread in all its cultural varieties.

World Spine Day highlights the importance of spinal health. Back and neck pain affect 1 in 10 people and are the leading cause of disability worldwide. The day promotes active and healthy lifestyles for spine care.

names.en: International Day for the Eradication of Poverty

descriptions.en: The International Day for the Eradication of Poverty has been observed since 1993. It provides an opportunity for all people, including those living in poverty, to come together to acknowledge their struggle.

slogans.en: Decent work and social protection: putting dignity into practice for all.

descriptions.en: World Menopause Day raises awareness of the menopause and the support options available for improving health and well-being for women in midlife and beyond. Millions of women experience menopause each year.

World Statistics Day, celebrated on October 20, highlights the importance of official statistics and promotes the fundamental principles of official statistics in an effort to improve the quality and understanding of data worldwide.

slogans.en: Connecting the World with Data We Can Trust.

descriptions.en: World Osteoporosis Day on October 20 launches a year-long campaign dedicated to raising global awareness of the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of osteoporosis.
The International Day of Statistics is observed on October 20 to celebrate the important role that statistics and data play in understanding our world and solving global challenges.

World Candy Day on October 20 is a delightful celebration of all things sweet. It's the perfect occasion to indulge your loved ones with their favorite treats, share chocolates and candies, and spread joy through the simple pleasure of sweets.

slogans.en: Life is sweeter when you share it.

descriptions.en: World Iodine Deficiency Day on October 21 aims to raise awareness about the importance of iodine in preventing thyroid disorders and promoting public health worldwide.

October 21 is celebrated as 'Back to the Future Day', the date Marty McFly and Doc Brown travelled to in the future in the 1985 blockbuster. Fans celebrate the iconic trilogy and its vision of the future.

slogans.en: Where we're going, we don't need roads.

descriptions.en: International Snow Leopard Day was established in 2014 when thirteen snow leopard range countries signed the Bishkek Declaration for snow leopard conservation. These elusive big cats are listed as vulnerable with only 4,000–6,500 remaining in the wild.

slogans.en: Ghost of the mountains needs our protection.

descriptions.en: United Nations Day is celebrated on October 24 each year to mark the anniversary of the entry into force of the UN Charter in 1945. The UN was founded to maintain international peace and security and to achieve international cooperation.

slogans.en: The future we want, the United Nations we need.

descriptions.en: World Origami Day (October 24) celebrates the Japanese art of paper folding. Origami transforms flat sheets of paper into sculptures through folding techniques and has evolved from ceremonial use into a mathematical art form practised worldwide.

slogans.en: One sheet of paper, endless possibilities.

descriptions.en: World Pasta Day on October 25 celebrates one of the world's most beloved foods. The World Pasta Congress established the day in 1995 to promote pasta as part of a healthy, balanced diet.
Austria's National Day on October 26 commemorates the Austrian Declaration of Neutrality in 1955, when Austria became a permanently neutral, democratic state following the State Treaty.

On October 27, families create a small ofrenda — an altar with photos, favourite toys, and treats — to welcome the spirits of their passed pets home for Día de los Muertos. A beautiful tradition that celebrates the bond between humans and animals beyond life.

slogans.en: Their spirit returns — light a candle, share a memory.

descriptions.en: Oxi Day on October 28 commemorates the rejection of Mussolini's ultimatum to Greece in 1940. Prime Minister Metaxas's legendary 'Oxi' (No) defiance against fascism is celebrated with parades across Greece.

slogans.en: Oxi! Greece Said No to Fascism.

descriptions.en: Republic Day is the most important national holiday in Turkey. It celebrates the proclamation of the Republic of Turkey on October 29, 1923, by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. The day is marked with ceremonies, parades, and fireworks throughout Turkey.

World Stroke Day on October 29 underscores the serious nature and high rates of stroke, raises awareness of the prevention and treatment of the condition, and ensures better care and support for survivors.
National Cat Day is celebrated in the United States on October 29 to raise awareness of the number of cats that need to be rescued each year and to celebrate cats as pets.

slogans.en: Every Cat Deserves a Loving Home

descriptions.en: Internet Day on October 29 commemorates the first transmission over the ARPANET on October 29, 1969, which was the precursor to the modern internet.

slogans.en: The World is Connected — Happy Internet Day!

descriptions.en: Halloween is celebrated each year on October 31. The tradition originated with the ancient Celtic festival of Samhain, when people would light bonfires and wear costumes to ward off ghosts. Today it involves costume parties, trick-or-treating, carving jack-o'-lanterns, and watching horror movies.

World Cities Day on October 31 promotes the international community's interest in global urbanization, pushes forward cooperation among countries in meeting opportunities and addressing challenges of urbanization.
World Handstand Day celebrates the skill of handstands and the discipline it takes to balance on your hands. People worldwide share their handstand photos and videos.

Reformation Day marks the anniversary of Martin Luther nailing his 95 Theses to the church door in Wittenberg on October 31, 1517. It is a public holiday in several predominantly Protestant German states.

slogans.en: Here I stand, I can do no other.

descriptions.en: World Savings Day (October 31) was established in 1924 at the first International Savings Bank Congress in Milan. It promotes saving money as a driver of economic security and financial independence for individuals and nations.

World Vegan Day is an annual event celebrated by vegans around the world every November 1. The event was established in 1994 by Louise Wallis to mark the 50th anniversary of the founding of the UK Vegan Society.

All Saints' Day honours all Christian saints and martyrs. It is a public holiday in the Catholic German states of Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria, North Rhine-Westphalia, Rhineland-Palatinate, and Saarland.

slogans.en: In memory of all who have gone before us.

descriptions.en: Culture Day (Bunka no Hi) on November 3 is a national holiday in Japan for the promotion of culture and love of freedom and peace. Ceremonies including art exhibitions and cultural events take place across the country.
World Tsunami Awareness Day on November 5 raises awareness about tsunamis and emphasizes the importance of early warning systems, disaster risk reduction and the need for preparedness.

Bonfire Night (Guy Fawkes Night) on November 5 commemorates the failure of the Gunpowder Plot of 1605 when Guy Fawkes attempted to blow up the Houses of Parliament. It is celebrated with bonfires and fireworks.

slogans.en: Remember, Remember the Fifth of November.

descriptions.en: National STEM Day (November 8) encourages students to explore and pursue interests in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. STEM education is critical for innovation and solving the world's greatest challenges.

slogans.en: Science + Technology + Engineering + Math = Our Future.

descriptions.en: On November 9, 1989, the Berlin Wall — the symbol of Cold War division — fell after the East German government announced that citizens could cross freely. Crowds flooded the checkpoints and began tearing down the wall. The event triggered the reunification of Germany and marked the symbolic end of the Cold War, becoming one of the most defining moments of the 20th century.

World Freedom Day is observed on November 9, the anniversary of the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989, which symbolized the end of the Cold War. It celebrates freedom from communism and totalitarianism.

slogans.en: Freedom is not free — cherish it.

descriptions.en: Carl Sagan Day celebrates the birthday of Carl Sagan (November 9, 1934), the legendary astronomer, author, and science communicator. Sagan made science accessible to millions through his TV series Cosmos and his book The Pale Blue Dot.

slogans.en: Somewhere, something incredible is waiting to be known.

names.en: World Science Day for Peace and Development

descriptions.en: World Science Day for Peace and Development highlights the significant role of science in society and the need to engage the wider public in debates on emerging scientific issues. It also underlines the importance of science and technology for sustainable development.

slogans.en: Open science for a global transformation.

descriptions.en: Remembrance Day (or Veterans Day in the US) is observed on November 11 to honor military veterans. It commemorates the armistice ending World War I at the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month of 1918.

Singles Day on November 11 (11/11) originated at Chinese universities in the 1990s as a celebration of being single, chosen because the date of 11/11 looks like four solitary individuals. It has since become the world's biggest online shopping event.
Poland's Independence Day on November 11 commemorates the restoration of Polish sovereignty in 1918 after over 100 years of partitions by Russia, Prussia, and Austria.

slogans.en: Jeszcze Polska nie zginęła! (Poland has not yet perished!)

descriptions.en: Armistice Day on November 11 marks the end of World War I, when the armistice signed at 11 am on November 11, 1918 came into force. France and Belgium observe it as a national holiday to honour fallen soldiers.

On 11/11 Turkey raises a glass of rakı — the anise-flavored national spirit. The date is a playful tradition: two tall rakı glasses placed beside two fish on a plate form the numbers '11 11', making it the perfect day to celebrate the beloved meze ritual.

slogans.en: Two glasses, two fish — cheers to tradition.

descriptions.en: World Kindness Day is a global day that promotes the importance of being kind to each other, to yourself, and to the world. It highlights good deeds in the community.

World Diabetes Day is the world's largest diabetes awareness campaign, reaching a global audience of over 1 billion people in more than 160 countries. The campaign draws attention to issues of paramount importance to the diabetes world. November 14 is the birthday of Frederick Banting, who discovered insulin.

The International Day for Tolerance was proclaimed in 1996 following UNESCO's Declaration of Principles on Tolerance of November 16, 1995. Tolerance is not only a moral duty, it is also a political and legal requirement.

slogans.en: Tolerance is not passive. It is an active recognition of universal human rights.

descriptions.en: World Prematurity Day on November 17 raises awareness of preterm birth and the concerns of premature babies and their families worldwide. Preterm birth is the leading cause of newborn deaths globally.

International Students' Day is observed on November 17 to commemorate the 1939 Nazi attack on Czech students and universities. It celebrates student activism worldwide and the right of all people to education.

slogans.en: Students are the future — protect their rights.

descriptions.en: World Antibiotic Awareness Week is an annual global campaign to raise awareness about antimicrobial resistance and to encourage responsible use of antibiotics.

International Men's Day is celebrated globally on November 19 each year. The objectives focus on men's and boys' health, improving gender relations, promoting gender equality, and highlighting positive male role models.

slogans.en: Helping men live longer, happier and more fulfilling lives.

descriptions.en: World Toilet Day on November 19 is an official United Nations international observance day that inspires action to tackle the global sanitation crisis. 3.6 billion people still live without access to safely managed sanitation.

Universal Children's Day was established in 1954 and is celebrated on November 20 each year. It promotes international togetherness, awareness among children worldwide, and improving children's welfare. November 20 is the date the UN adopted the Declaration of the Rights of the Child in 1959.

World Children's Day is celebrated on 20 November. It was established in 1954 and marks the date on which the UN General Assembly adopted the Declaration of the Rights of the Child in 1959, and the Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1989.

slogans.en: A World Fit for Every Child.

descriptions.en: Mexican Revolution Day commemorates the beginning of the Mexican Revolution on November 20, 1910. It is a national holiday marked by parades and civic events throughout Mexico.

slogans.en: Viva la Revolución! — Celebrating Mexican Heritage

descriptions.en: The Transgender Day of Remembrance (TDOR) is observed annually to memorialize those who were killed due to anti-transgender hatred or prejudice. It was founded in 1999 by Gwendolyn Ann Smith to honor Rita Hester.

slogans.en: Remembering our trans family who are no longer with us.

descriptions.en: Africa Industrialization Day (November 20) mobilizes the commitment of the international community to the industrialization of Africa. It highlights the continent's potential for industrial development and economic transformation.

World Television Day on November 21 was proclaimed by the UN in 1996. It represents a symbol not so much of entertainment but of communication and globalization, and television is seen as a way to spotlight conflicts and threats to peace and security.

slogans.en: TV: A Window to the World.

descriptions.en: World Philosophy Day is celebrated every third Thursday of November. Proclaimed by UNESCO in 2002, it highlights the enduring value of philosophy for the development of human thought and for addressing fundamental questions about the world.

World Hello Day on November 21 was created in response to the conflict between Egypt and Israel in 1973. Participants greet ten people that day, demonstrating that personal communication is the fundamental to world peace.

Fibonacci Day on November 23 (11/23) celebrates the famous Fibonacci sequence where each number is the sum of the two preceding ones (1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8...). The date 11/23 mirrors the beginning of this sequence found throughout nature.

names.en: International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women

descriptions.en: This day marks the beginning of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence. It's a time to call on governments, institutions, and individuals to take action to end gender-based violence — a global human rights violation that claims the lives of 1 in 3 women.

slogans.en: UNiTE! Invest to prevent violence against women and girls.

descriptions.en: Thanksgiving Day in the United States is celebrated on the fourth Thursday of November. It commemorates a 1621 harvest feast shared between English colonists and the Wampanoag people, and has evolved into a day of gratitude.

slogans.en: Grateful for Everything. Thankful for Everyone.

descriptions.en: Computer Security Day has been celebrated since 1988, originally to raise awareness and increase the protection of computers. Today it serves as a reminder to protect personal and business data through strong passwords, updates, and security awareness.

slogans.en: Protect your data. Protect your life.

descriptions.en: St. Andrew's Day is the feast day of Saint Andrew, the patron saint of Scotland, celebrated on November 30 with Scottish cultural events and traditions.

slogans.en: Scotland the Brave — Happy St. Andrew's Day!

descriptions.en: World AIDS Day, observed on December 1 each year, is dedicated to raising awareness of the AIDS pandemic caused by the spread of HIV infection. The red ribbon is the symbol of World AIDS Day.

Romania's National Day on December 1 commemorates the unification of Transylvania with the Kingdom of Romania in 1918, creating Greater Romania. The day is celebrated with military parades in Bucharest.

names.en: International Day for the Abolition of Slavery

descriptions.en: The International Day for the Abolition of Slavery commemorates the date the UN adopted the Supplementary Convention on the Abolition of Slavery in 1956. It focuses on eradicating contemporary forms of slavery including human trafficking and child labor.

names.en: International Day of Persons with Disabilities

descriptions.en: The International Day of Persons with Disabilities has been observed since 1992. It aims to promote the rights and well-being of persons with disabilities in all spheres of society and development. Over 1 billion people in the world live with some form of disability.

slogans.en: United in action to rescue and achieve the SDGs for, with and by persons with disabilities.

descriptions.en: World Cookie Day on December 4 is a sweet celebration dedicated to everyone's favourite baked treat. Whether chocolate chip, oatmeal raisin, or gingerbread, it is a day to bake and share cookies with friends and family.

slogans.en: Life is Short, Eat More Cookies.

descriptions.en: National Cookie Day on December 4 is a delicious celebration of everyone's favorite baked treats. Share cookies with friends, family, and neighbors on this sweet holiday.

slogans.en: Life is Short, Eat More Cookies!

descriptions.en: World Wildlife Conservation Day was created by Hillary Clinton in 2012 to bring attention to the global wildlife crisis. It focuses on stopping illegal wildlife trade and protecting endangered species from extinction.

slogans.en: Wildlife crime is a global crisis.

descriptions.en: International Volunteer Day offers a unique chance for volunteers and organisations to celebrate their efforts, share their values, and promote their work among their communities, NGOs, UN agencies, government authorities and the private sector.

slogans.en: If everyone did a little, we could achieve a lot.

descriptions.en: World Soil Day is used to focus attention on the importance of healthy soil and to advocate for the sustainable management of soil resources. Healthy soils are essential for growing food, providing clean water, and supporting biodiversity.
Thailand's National Day on December 5 celebrates the birthday of the late King Bhumibol Adulyadej (Rama IX), who passed away in 2016. It is also observed as Father's Day in Thailand.

slogans.en: Long Live Thailand — Land of Smiles.

descriptions.en: Krampusnacht (December 5) is the night before St. Nicholas Day in Alpine tradition. Krampus, a horned creature from Germanic folklore, accompanies St. Nicholas and punishes naughty children while Nicholas rewards the good.

On the evening of December 5, children in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland place their boots outside the door. On the morning of December 6, St. Nicholas (Nikolaus) has filled them with sweets, nuts, and small gifts for good children — or left birch twigs for naughty ones. The tradition dates to the feast day of Saint Nicholas of Myra, patron saint of children, and is one of the most beloved winter customs in German-speaking countries.

slogans.en: Good things come to those who are kind.

descriptions.en: Finnish Independence Day commemorates the Declaration of Independence of Finland from Russia in 1917. It is one of the most important public holidays in Finland, celebrated with official receptions, ceremonies, and placing candles in windows.

The International Anti-Corruption Day was established in December 2003 to raise awareness about corruption. The United Nations estimates that corruption costs the global economy $2.6 trillion — or 5% of global GDP — each year.

Human Rights Day is observed every year on December 10 — the date in 1948 when the UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. This document proclaims the inalienable rights that everyone is entitled to as a human being.

slogans.en: Our rights, our future, right now.

descriptions.en: Nobel Prize Day, December 10, marks the anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death in 1896. On this day, Nobel Prize laureates receive their awards in Stockholm and Oslo in formal ceremonies recognizing extraordinary contributions to humanity.

International Mountain Day was created in 2003 to encourage international community to organize events to highlight the importance of mountains. Mountains cover about 27% of the Earth's land surface and provide freshwater for over half of humanity.

National Tango Day in Argentina (December 11) celebrates the birthday of Carlos Gardel, the iconic tango singer. The tango, born in the Rio de la Plata region, is a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage and embodies Argentine national identity.

slogans.en: Let the rhythm of tango move your soul.

descriptions.en: Jamhuri Day on December 12 marks Kenya's independence from British colonial rule in 1963 and the country's proclamation as a republic in 1964. 'Jamhuri' means 'republic' in Swahili.
Kenya's Independence Day (Jamhuri Day) on December 12 marks the country's independence from British rule in 1963. It is celebrated with music, dance, and national pride.

International Migrants Day is observed on December 18 to recognize the large and increasing number of migrants in the world. It aims to advocate for the rights of migrants and promote their contributions to society.

slogans.en: Harnessing the potential of human mobility.

descriptions.en: World Arabic Language Day (December 18) celebrates the Arabic language and its historical and cultural role in human civilization. Arabic is spoken by over 400 million people and is one of the six official languages of the United Nations.

slogans.en: Arabic: a language of history, beauty, and wisdom.

descriptions.en: Yule is an ancient winter solstice festival with Norse and Germanic origins, celebrated around December 21. It marks the return of the sun after the longest night of the year and is a time for feasting, gift-giving, and honoring nature's cycles.

slogans.en: The sun returns — light conquers darkness.

descriptions.en: La Noche de Rábanos (Night of the Radishes) is a unique Mexican festival held in Oaxaca on December 23. Artisans carve elaborate scenes from giant radishes depicting nativity scenes, local legends, and historical events.

Jólabókaflóð (Christmas Book Flood) is an Icelandic tradition where books are exchanged as Christmas Eve gifts, then people spend the night reading. Iceland publishes more books per capita than any nation and the tradition dates to World War II when paper was one of the few unrationed goods.

slogans.en: A book as a gift — the best Christmas tradition.

descriptions.en: Christmas is celebrated by billions of people worldwide, both as a religious holiday marking the birth of Jesus Christ and as a cultural and family celebration. Traditions include gift giving, caroling, decorating Christmas trees, and gathering with family.

slogans.en: Peace on earth and goodwill to all.

descriptions.en: The Second Day of Christmas is a public holiday in all German states. Families continue their Christmas celebrations, visit relatives, and attend church services.

Kwanzaa is a week-long celebration from December 26 to January 1 honoring African heritage in African-American culture. Created in 1966 by Maulana Karenga, it celebrates seven core principles: unity, self-determination, collective work, cooperative economics, purpose, creativity, and faith.

slogans.en: Seven days, seven principles — the spirit of African heritage.

descriptions.en: New Year's Eve is the last day of the year, celebrated in most countries of the world. Festivities include public and private events, fireworks displays, and parties that last until after midnight when the New Year begins.

slogans.en: Out with the old, in with the new.

descriptions.en: Regaib Kandili is observed on the night before the first Friday of Rajab, the seventh month of the Islamic calendar. It marks the night Muhammad's parents are said to have conceived him. In Turkey it is one of the five holy nights (Kandil geceleri) observed with special prayers, mosque visits, and the lighting of minarets.

slogans.en: Bu mübarek gecede kalpler huzur bulur.

descriptions.en: Thaipusam is a Hindu festival celebrated mainly in southern India, Malaysia, Singapore, and Sri Lanka. Devotees honor the god Murugan by undertaking elaborate rituals of devotion, often carrying kavadis or performing body piercings.

Up Helly Aa is a fire festival held annually in Lerwick, Shetland, Scotland on the last Tuesday of January. It celebrates Shetland's Viking heritage with torch-lit processions culminating in the burning of a Viking longship.

slogans.en: Fire and Viking spirit ignite the night.

descriptions.en: Miraç Kandili commemorates the Isra and Mi'raj — the night journey and ascension of the Prophet Muhammad from Mecca to Jerusalem and then to the heavens. Observed on the 27th of Rajab, it is one of the most significant nights in the Islamic calendar. In Turkey mosques hold special prayers, Quranic recitations, and minarets are illuminated throughout the night.

slogans.en: Göklere yükselen o gece nur oldu.

descriptions.en: The Lantern Festival marks the final day of the Chinese New Year celebrations on the 15th day of the first lunar month. People light lanterns, solve riddles written on lanterns, eat tangyuan (sweet rice balls), and watch lion dances.

slogans.en: Light up the night — the new year's final glow.

descriptions.en: Berat Kandili is observed on the 15th night of Sha'ban, the eighth month of the Islamic calendar. It is believed that on this night God determines the fate of all living beings for the coming year and forgives those who seek repentance. In Turkey it is observed with night-long prayers, fasting, and visits to cemeteries to pray for the deceased.

slogans.en: Affın kapıları bu gece sonuna kadar açık.

descriptions.en: Pink Shirt Day is an anti-bullying day celebrated on the last Wednesday in February. It started in Canada in 2007 when two students stood against bullying by wearing pink shirts. Today millions around the world wear pink to take a stand.

Rare Disease Day takes place on the last day of February to raise awareness of rare diseases and their impact on patients' lives. Over 300 million people worldwide are living with one of the 6,000 rare diseases known to science.

slogans.en: Share your colours — rare is many, rare is strong.

descriptions.en: Open Data Day is an annual celebration of open data held on the first Saturday of March. People worldwide create events, host workshops, and publish analyses to show the benefits of open data for society, government, and research.

slogans.en: Open data for open government and open society.

descriptions.en: Mothering Sunday is a UK tradition celebrated on the fourth Sunday of Lent. Originally a day for people to return to their 'mother church', it evolved into a celebration of mothers and is distinct from the American Mother's Day tradition.

slogans.en: For all the love our mothers give.

descriptions.en: Commonwealth Day is observed on the second Monday of March. It is the main annual celebration for the 56 member countries of the Commonwealth of Nations, promoting international understanding and cooperation across a community of 2.4 billion people.

World Kidney Day is a global awareness campaign aimed at raising awareness about the importance of kidneys and reducing the frequency and impact of kidney disease worldwide. It falls on the second Thursday in March.

Red Nose Day is a fundraising event organized by Comic Relief in the UK, held every two years. People wear red noses and do funny things to raise money for charities fighting poverty and injustice in the UK and Africa.

slogans.en: We're all in this together — do something funny for money.

descriptions.en: World Social Work Day celebrates the achievements of social workers globally and highlights social work's contribution to human well-being. It falls on the third Tuesday in March each year.
Good Friday commemorates the crucifixion of Jesus Christ, observed on the Friday before Easter Sunday. It is a silent, solemn public holiday across all of Germany.

Easter Sunday celebrates the resurrection of Jesus Christ, the central feast of the Christian year. In Germany it is a public holiday and families gather for festive meals, painted egg hunts, and church services.
Easter Monday is the day after Easter Sunday, celebrating the resurrection of Jesus Christ. It is a national public holiday in all German states.

Laylat al-Qadr — Kadir Gecesi in Turkish — is the holiest night of the Islamic year, falling in the last ten nights of Ramadan, traditionally on the 27th. The Quran describes it as 'better than a thousand months'. Muslims spend the night in prayer believing their supplications are especially answered. In Turkey, mosques are packed with worshippers and minarets glow throughout the night.

Eid al-Fitr — called Ramazan Bayramı or Şeker Bayramı (Sugar Festival) in Turkey — marks the end of Ramadan, the month of fasting. It is celebrated for three days with family gatherings, special sweets (especially Turkish delight and baklava), new clothes, and visits to relatives. Children receive gifts and kisses on the hand from elders, who offer candy in return.

The International Day of Pink is a Canadian anti-bullying observance celebrated on the second Wednesday in April. It supports LGBTQ+ students and speaks out against bullying, discrimination, and homophobia in schools.

International Guide Dog Day raises awareness about the incredible work of guide dogs and the organizations that train them. Guide dogs provide independence, safety, and companionship for people who are blind or visually impaired.

slogans.en: Guide dogs — independence and loyalty in one.

descriptions.en: World Password Day is observed on the first Thursday in May to promote better password habits. Strong, unique passwords are the first line of defense against cyberattacks in an era where data breaches affect billions of people.

slogans.en: A strong password is your best defence.

descriptions.en: Ascension Day marks Jesus Christ's ascension into heaven, celebrated 39 days after Easter Sunday. It is also traditionally Father's Day (Vatertag) in Germany.
Pentecost Sunday marks the descent of the Holy Spirit upon the apostles, 49 days after Easter. Together with Whit Monday it forms a two-day public holiday weekend in Germany.

slogans.en: The spirit is poured out on all people.

descriptions.en: Whit Monday follows Pentecost Sunday, 50 days after Easter. It commemorates the descent of the Holy Spirit and is a public holiday throughout Germany.

slogans.en: The spirit moves through all things.

descriptions.en: Victoria Day is a Canadian public holiday observed on the last Monday before or on May 25, celebrating the birthday of Queen Victoria (May 24, 1819). It also unofficially marks the beginning of summer in Canada with fireworks and outdoor festivities.

slogans.en: May long weekend — summer begins in Canada!

descriptions.en: Corpus Christi celebrates the Eucharist, observed 60 days after Easter. It is a public holiday in the predominantly Catholic German states of Bavaria, Baden-Württemberg, Hesse, North Rhine-Westphalia, Rhineland-Palatinate, and Saarland.

Eid al-Adha — Kurban Bayramı in Turkey — commemorates the willingness of Ibrahim to sacrifice his son as an act of obedience to God. It is celebrated for four days. Families who can afford it sacrifice a sheep, cow, or goat, and distribute the meat to neighbours, relatives, and those in need. It is one of the two major Islamic festivals and a public holiday in Turkey.

Vardavar is an Armenian summer festival where people drench each other with water. Originating from a pre-Christian feast dedicated to the goddess Astghik, the festival is now celebrated 98 days after Easter with joyful water fights.

slogans.en: Cool down with joy — happy Vardavar!

descriptions.en: World Calligraphy Day is observed on the second Wednesday of August to celebrate the art of beautiful handwriting across diverse cultural traditions. From Chinese brushwork to Arabic scripts to Western lettering, calligraphy is a timeless art form.

slogans.en: Every letter, a stroke of art.

descriptions.en: World Honey Bee Day is celebrated on the third Saturday of August to promote awareness about the importance of bees and sustainable beekeeping. Bees pollinate one-third of the food we eat and are essential for ecosystem health.

slogans.en: Save the bees, save the world.

descriptions.en: The Hungry Ghost Festival is a traditional Chinese and Buddhist/Taoist festival observed on the 15th day of the seventh month in the lunar calendar. It is believed that the spirits of the deceased roam the Earth, and offerings are made to honor them.

La Tomatina is a festival held in Buñol, Spain on the last Wednesday of August, where participants throw tomatoes at each other in a massive food fight. The tradition began spontaneously in 1945 and now attracts thousands of participants worldwide.

R U OK? Day is an Australian suicide prevention initiative held on the second Thursday in September. It encourages people to meaningfully connect with those around them and start a conversation with anyone who may be struggling.

slogans.en: Are you ok? Ask someone today.

descriptions.en: Mevlid Kandili celebrates the birthday of the Prophet Muhammad on the 12th of Rabi' al-Awwal. In Turkey it is a deeply observed holy night. The tradition of the Mevlid — a poem praising the Prophet written by Süleyman Çelebi in 1409 — is recited in mosques across the country. Families gather, special prayers are held, and minarets are illuminated.

International Coastal Cleanup Day is the world's largest volunteer effort to protect the ocean. Organized by Ocean Conservancy, millions of volunteers clean beaches and waterways worldwide on the third Saturday in September.

Batman Day is observed on the third Saturday of September to celebrate the anniversary of Batman's creation. First introduced in Detective Comics #27 in 1939, Batman is one of the world's most iconic and enduring superheroes.

slogans.en: I am the night. I am Batman.

descriptions.en: World Rivers Day is a celebration of the world's waterways observed on the fourth Sunday of September. It highlights the value of rivers and promotes efforts to protect them from pollution, over-extraction, and climate change.

slogans.en: Celebrate our rivers — protect their future.

descriptions.en: Native American Day honors the rich history, culture, and contributions of Indigenous peoples of the United States. Observed on the fourth Friday of September in California and other states, it celebrates tribal heritage and advocates for Indigenous rights.

slogans.en: Honor the past, celebrate the present, build the future.

descriptions.en: Ada Lovelace Day celebrates the achievements of women in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. Ada Lovelace (1815–1852) is widely regarded as the world's first computer programmer for her work on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine.

slogans.en: Inspiring women in STEM, one pioneer at a time.

descriptions.en: World Quality Day is observed on the second Thursday of November to raise awareness about quality in organizations and its contribution to business success, sustainability, and improved outcomes for people.

slogans.en: Quality — doing it right the first time.

descriptions.en: Loy Krathong is a Thai festival held on the full moon of the 12th month of the traditional Thai lunar calendar. People float decorated baskets (krathong) on water as offerings to the water goddess and to let go of negativity.

slogans.en: Float away the worries, welcome the light.

descriptions.en: World COPD Day is organized by the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) to improve awareness and care for COPD patients. It falls on the third Wednesday of November each year.

Stir-Up Sunday is the last Sunday before Advent, the traditional day in Britain for making Christmas pudding. Each family member stirs the pudding mixture from East to West, making a secret wish, following a Victorian tradition.

slogans.en: Stir, wish, and let Christmas magic begin.

descriptions.en: Buy Nothing Day is an international day of protest against consumerism, observed on the day after US Thanksgiving (Black Friday). Participants are encouraged to stop buying for 24 hours and reflect on environmental and social impacts of overconsumption.

slogans.en: 24 hours of not spending — can you do it?

descriptions.en: National Wine Day on May 25th celebrates wine in all its glorious forms—red, white, rosé, and sparkling. With roots dating back to at least 2009, this grassroots holiday honors wine’s ancient history (the oldest evidence of winemaking dates to 7000 BC) and its enduring role in culture and cuisine. Raise a glass with friends, explore new varietals, and discover the art of food and wine pairing.

slogans.en: Raise a glass to the world’s oldest pleasure.

descriptions.en: World Redhead Day on May 26th celebrates one of nature's rarest hair colors — found in only 1–2% of the world's population. What began with Dutch artist Bart Rouwenhorst's 2005 casting call for red-haired models, which unexpectedly drew huge crowds, grew into annual Redhead Days festivals in the Netherlands and eventually a global movement. The day champions red hair in all its shades — from strawberry blonde to deep auburn — and turns what was once a target for teasing into a source of community pride.

slogans.en: Be rare, be radiant — embrace your red.

descriptions.en: Brunettes Day on May 28th is a lighthearted celebration of dark-haired people around the world. While its exact origins are unclear, it has gained momentum on social media as a counterpart to other hair color observances. Brunette hair — ranging from dark blonde to nearly black — is the most common hair color globally, making this a day for the majority to celebrate what they sometimes take for granted.

slogans.en: Dark hair, bright spirit — today is yours.

descriptions.en: Blonde Hair Day on May 31st celebrates one of the world's most iconic hair colors and its rich genetic and cultural history. Blonde hair traces back 17,000 years to Siberia and has been immortalized in art, cinema, and culture — from Jean Harlow's platinum locks to countless modern icons. In 2014 scientists pinpointed the exact genetic switch: a single nucleotide change in the KITLG gene. Natural or color-treated, today is a day to embrace the gold.

slogans.en: Golden roots, timeless style — celebrate your light.

descriptions.en: World Tattoo Day on March 21st celebrates the history, artistry, and cultural significance of tattoos. Established in 2015 to connect tattoo and body artists worldwide, the date was chosen for its layered symbolism: the spring equinox, International Color Day, and Harmony Day. Tattoos have ancient roots — evidence dates back to 3000 BCE — and have evolved from markers of status and identity across civilisations into a widely celebrated art form.

slogans.en: Every tattoo tells a story — wear yours with pride.

descriptions.en: A day dedicated to celebrating the special bond between best friends — those people who always have your back through laughter, tears, and everything in between.

slogans.en: Side by side or miles apart, best friends are always close at heart.

descriptions.en: National Cancer Thriver Day honors those who have faced cancer and continue to live with strength, purpose, and hope. Founded by Connect4Cancer in 2021, the day celebrates active, engaged living after cancer — not just survival, but thriving through grit, resilience, and deep meaning.

Christopher Street Day commemorates the Stonewall Uprising of June 28, 1969, when LGBTQ+ people and allies stood up against police harassment outside the Stonewall Inn in New York City. Celebrated mainly across Germany, Switzerland, and Austria, it blends colorful parades with activism for visibility, equality, and community.

slogans.en: Pride, visibility, and equal rights for all.

descriptions.en: International Body Piercing Day celebrates body modification as a form of self-expression and personal identity. It honors Jim Ward, often called the granddaddy of the modern piercing movement, who pioneered techniques in the Western world. From ancient tribal traditions to today's studios, the day encourages people to explore piercing as a meaningful way to express individuality.

slogans.en: Express yourself, one piercing at a time.

descriptions.en: Log Cabin Day, observed on the last Sunday of June, honors the log cabin as a symbol of early American life and the pioneering spirit. Started in Michigan in 1986 by the Log Cabin Society and Bad Axe Historical Society, it celebrates the craftsmanship and resilience of early settlers through tours, educational programs, and preservation of these historic structures.

slogans.en: Honoring the pioneering spirit, one log at a time.

descriptions.en: Insurance Awareness Day, observed annually on June 28, encourages people to review their coverage, learn about policy options, and protect their homes, cars, health, and loved ones. It serves as a reminder that coverage needs change over time. Insurance has ancient roots, appearing in the Code of Hammurabi and evolving into modern property insurance after the Great Fire of London in 1666.

slogans.en: Review, protect, and plan for peace of mind.

descriptions.en: World Industrial Design Day celebrates the designers who shape the everyday products around us. Founded by the World Design Organization in 2007 to mark 50 years since ICSID, it highlights how thoughtful design drives social, cultural, and economic progress and raises awareness of the industrial design profession.

Hug Holiday, established by the Hugs 4 Health Foundation, celebrates the power of warm, consensual hugs to nurture connection and well-being. It was created to address touch deprivation, especially among seniors in care, and to promote the documented benefits of supportive physical contact like lower stress and greater emotional resilience.

slogans.en: A warm hug heals more than words.

descriptions.en: St. Peter's Day honors one of Jesus' closest followers and the first leader of the Church, celebrating his journey from fisherman to bold spiritual leader. Christians mark it with worship services, coastal blessings, and community gatherings, with especially grand ceremonies in Rome. The feast dates to early Christian Rome and was in religious calendars by the fourth century.

slogans.en: From fisherman to the rock of faith.

descriptions.en: International Fisherman Day honors the people who make their living from fishing, celebrating their skill, stamina, and the importance of seafood to global food security. Often linked to June 29 because Saint Peter is a patron of fishers, it highlights the vital role of small-scale fisheries and the need for sustainable, responsible ocean stewardship.

slogans.en: Honoring those who feed the world from the sea.

descriptions.en: Wimbledon is one of the most iconic and prestigious tennis tournaments in the world, famous for its grass courts, all-white dress code, and timeless traditions. Founded in 1877 by the All England Club with just 22 male players, it added women's singles and men's doubles in 1884 and has grown into a beloved sporting event that draws top players and the British Royal Family each summer.

slogans.en: Grass, grit, and glory on Centre Court.

descriptions.en: International Joke Day celebrates humor and laughter by encouraging people to share jokes with friends, family, and even strangers. It highlights the health benefits of laughter, from lower stress to a brighter mood. Jokes have ancient roots—the Greeks recorded some of the first and even hosted early comedy gatherings.

slogans.en: Share a laugh, brighten someone's day.

descriptions.en: Made In The USA Day celebrates American-made products and domestic manufacturing, encouraging consumers to support goods produced at home. It was established in 1989 by Joel Joseph of the Made in the USA Foundation to highlight manufacturing's economic importance. The Federal Trade Commission oversees the labels that mark a product's country of origin.

National Bikini Day commemorates the invention of the bikini in 1946 by Parisian designer Louis Réard, and celebrates fun in the sun and the freedom to choose one's own swimwear. Before its arrival, swimwear was strictly modest—"beach police" once policed hemlines—so the bikini marked a cultural turning point toward personal freedom and body confidence.

slogans.en: Sun, sand, and the freedom to shine.

descriptions.en: National Fried Chicken Day celebrates one of the world's most beloved comfort foods, enjoyed at restaurants, home kitchens, and gatherings alike. Fried chicken has ancient roots—it appears in Roman cookbooks—but took its iconic form in America through a blend of Scottish and West African traditions. Once a delicacy, it became a global staple after the Second World War.

slogans.en: Crispy, golden, and impossible to resist.

descriptions.en: National Video Game Day celebrates the gaming industry and its huge cultural impact, inviting fans to play, host parties, and dive into video game trivia. The observance emerged in the early 1990s, with the first recorded celebration around 1991. From arcades to consoles to mobile and cloud gaming, it honors a hobby enjoyed by billions worldwide.

Independence From Meat Day invites people to skip meat for a day and discover the benefits of vegetarian and vegan eating. Founded by the Vegetarian Awareness Network in Knoxville, Tennessee, it falls on July 4th to offer a plant-based contrast to America's biggest grilling holiday. It spotlights the health and environmental case for cutting back on meat, from greenhouse gases to water and land use.

slogans.en: One day, no meat, all the flavor.

names.en: Don't Step On A Bee Day

descriptions.en: Don't Step On A Bee Day reminds us to protect bees from accidental harm and to support their conservation. It highlights the vital role bees play in pollination and food production. Founded by Ruth and Thomas Roy, it has grown alongside global concern over declining bee populations, which have dropped sharply in some regions in recent decades.

slogans.en: Watch your step, save a bee.

descriptions.en: All-American Pet Photo Day encourages pet owners to snap photos of their companions and share them online. It celebrates the joy pets bring and the special bond between people and their animals. With no documented founder, it has grown into a beloved annual tradition that inspires pet lovers to capture their animals' unique personalities.

slogans.en: Snap it, share it, love your pet.

descriptions.en: Barn Day, held on the second Sunday in July, celebrates barns as the heart of farm communities—vital spaces for animals, hay, tools, and shared memories. It brings farmers and neighbors together through farm tours and community events that honor rural heritage. The observance grew from early barn-raising traditions, when communities gathered to build barns cooperatively.

slogans.en: Where community, heritage, and hard work meet.

descriptions.en: Cow Appreciation Day, on the second Tuesday in July, celebrates cows and their contributions to food and agriculture. It began in 1995 as a playful Chick-fil-A campaign built around cows urging people to "Eat Mor Chikin." The quirky idea grew into an annual tradition where fans dress up as cows for fun and free food at participating restaurants.

slogans.en: Moo-ve over and celebrate the cows.

descriptions.en: Thirsty Thursday, on the first Thursday in July, is all about enjoying favorite beverages and socializing with friends as an early start to the weekend. The term originated in Minor League Baseball, coined in 1983 by Ron McKee of the Asheville Tourists. It spread through college culture and into workplaces as people embraced a little midweek merriment.

slogans.en: Cheers to an early start on the weekend.

descriptions.en: National Soccer Day celebrates the beautiful game—a global passion built on skill, teamwork, and the thrill of scoring goals. Established in 1994, it honors the players, coaches, and fans of one of the world's most widely played sports. Soccer's modern rules took shape in 1800s London, though ball games resembling it date back thousands of years.

slogans.en: One ball, one world, endless passion.

descriptions.en: National Outfit-of-the-Day Day celebrates personal style and the confidence that comes from putting together a look you love. Founded by Stassi Schroeder in 2018, it grew out of fashion blogging and #OOTD culture, encouraging people to share their daily outfits online. It turns getting dressed into a small, joyful act of self-expression.

slogans.en: Style it your way, own the day.

descriptions.en: World Snorkeling Day celebrates one of the most accessible ways to explore the underwater world—just a mask, a tube, and fins turn the ocean into a living window. Snorkelers can watch reefs, fish, and turtles up close without the training scuba demands. Emerging through travel communities in the mid-2010s, it also champions ocean awareness and reef protection.

National Meteor Watch Day celebrates the science and wonder of shooting stars—bright streaks made as meteoroids burn up in Earth's atmosphere. It invites people to look up, learn, and share the night sky with loved ones. The date echoes the 1908 Tunguska event, a massive blast believed to be caused by a meteoroid that flattened millions of trees.

slogans.en: Look up and make a wish.

descriptions.en: Queer Youth of Faith Day celebrates and supports LGBTQ+ young people navigating their faith communities. Established in 2019 by the nonprofit Beloved Arise, it is the first national U.S. observance dedicated to empowering queer youth of faith. It works to build affirming spaces, offer support, and show that spiritual and queer identities can be lived authentically together.

Suicide Prevention Month, observed throughout September, raises awareness of suicide as a major and preventable public health issue.
