It encourages open conversations about mental health, reduces stigma, and points people toward support and crisis resources. The month reminds everyone that reaching out, checking in, and listening can save lives.

slogans.en: Reach out, check in, save a life.

descriptions.en: LGBTQ+ History Month celebrates the achievements, struggles, and trailblazers of the lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer community. Founded in 1994 by U.S. teacher Rodney Wilson, it is observed in October in the United States, timed around National Coming Out Day, while the UK marks it in February. It provides role models and educates about LGBTQ+ contributions to society.

slogans.en: Remembering the past, inspiring the future.

descriptions.en: Harvey Milk Day honors the birthday and legacy of Harvey Milk, the first openly gay person elected to public office in California. Made a state holiday in 2009, it celebrates his pioneering role in LGBTQ+ rights through education, flag-raisings, and advocacy. Elected to San Francisco's Board of Supervisors in 1977, Milk was assassinated in 1978 but remains an enduring symbol of hope.

Wildland Firefighter Week of Remembrance, held June 30 to July 6, honors the wildland firefighters who lost their lives battling wildfires. It asks us to remember them by their names and stories, not as statistics. Established in 2014, the week spans the anniversaries of the 2013 Yarnell Hill Fire, which claimed nineteen Granite Mountain Hotshots, and the 1994 South Canyon Fire.

Be a Kid Again Day encourages adults to reconnect with their inner child through play, curiosity, and simple delights. As George Bernard Shaw put it, "we don't stop playing because we grow old; we grow old because we stop playing." Founded in 1990 by Atari creator Nolan Bushnell, it's a yearly nudge to swap stress for wonder.

Fashion Day celebrates personal style and the creativity of expressing yourself through clothing and accessories. Started in 2016 as a grassroots social-media movement, it was framed as a gentle revolt against fashion dictated by big houses, prioritizing individual creativity over trends. It encourages everyone to define and show off their own style.

National Kitten Day celebrates kittens and raises awareness for the many that need rescue and homes. Founded in 2012 by pet behaviorist Colleen Paige, it encourages adoption, volunteering, and donations to cat charities. Moved from December to July to align with peak kitten season, it also promotes spaying and neutering to ease overpopulation.

World Kebab Day, on the second Friday in July, celebrates the beloved grilled meat and vegetable dish on skewers that unites culinary traditions across the globe. Kebabs originated in the Middle East and spread along trade routes through Central Asia, giving rise to favorites like shish and doner. The day invites restaurant visits, barbecues, and creative homemade kebabs.

National Financial Freedom Day encourages people to pursue financial independence through smart money management, budgeting, and investing. It champions the idea of letting your savings and investments do the heavy lifting so you can live life on your own terms. The day is a yearly reminder to review goals, build good habits, and work toward freedom from financial stress.

slogans.en: Make your money work for you.

descriptions.en: July Morning is a beloved Bulgarian tradition where thousands gather at the coast and in the mountains to welcome the first sunrise of July. More than dawn-watching, it symbolizes freedom, hope, and fresh starts, mixing rock music, camping, and community. It began in the late 1970s as a quiet act of defiance under communism and took its name from a British rock anthem.

slogans.en: Greet the dawn, embrace the freedom.

names.en: National Stay Out of the Sun Day

descriptions.en: National Stay Out of the Sun Day encourages people to give their skin a break by staying indoors or seeking shade. It raises awareness of UV damage, which can cause sunburn, premature aging, and skin cancer—one of the most common cancers in young adults. The day is a practical reminder to enjoy summer safely with shade, cover-ups, and sunscreen.

slogans.en: Give your skin a break today.

descriptions.en: National Pet Fire Safety Day encourages pet owners to make safety plans and fire-proof their homes to protect their animals. Around 500,000 pets are affected by home fires each year, making prevention and preparedness essential. Established in 2009 by the American Kennel Club and ADT Security Services, it highlights both the risks pets face and hazards they can accidentally create.

Sweetness Week (Semana de la Dulzura) is a much-loved Argentine tradition held July 1–7, when people give a sweet or candy in exchange for a kiss. It started in 1989 as a candy-brand marketing campaign and grew into a nationwide celebration of affection, friendship, and small gestures. Across the week, friends, couples, and coworkers swap treats and kisses to share a little sweetness.

slogans.en: A sweet for a kiss, all week long.

descriptions.en: National Picnic Month, celebrated throughout July, invites everyone outdoors to share meals in nature during the warm summer days. It honors the simple joy of gathering with family and friends in parks and green spaces to eat, relax, and make memories. The word "picnic" dates back centuries, and the tradition has united people from family outings to historic mass gatherings.

National Ice Cream Month celebrates America's favorite frozen treat throughout the hottest month of the year. It encourages enjoying ice cream in every form—cones, bowls, sundaes, and pairings with pie or brownies. The designation was made official by President Ronald Reagan and the American Dairy Association, turning a sweet indulgence into a month-long national celebration.

slogans.en: Scoop up summer, one cone at a time.

descriptions.en: National Anti-Boredom Month, observed in July, is dedicated to beating the summer slump that often follows the Independence Day excitement. It encourages people of all ages to try new hobbies, volunteer, and seek out fresh experiences that stimulate the mind and body. Created by Alan Caruba in the 1980s, it also celebrates how a little boredom can spark creativity and new ideas.

World Sports Journalists Day honors the reporters who turn sporting events into compelling stories that bring fans closer to the action. Sports journalists do more than share scores—they shape how we see the game through coverage, analysis, and features. It was established in 1994 to mark the 70th anniversary of the International Sports Press Association (AIPS), founded at the 1924 Paris Olympics.

slogans.en: Bringing the game to life, story by story.

descriptions.en: National Disco Day celebrates the vibrant grooves and inclusive spirit of disco music and culture, inviting everyone to dance and dress in retro style. Disco emerged in the late 1960s from underground clubs serving Black, Latino, and LGBTQ+ communities in New York, where DJs blended soul, funk, and Latin sounds. The day itself began in 2014, created by New Zealand music fans to honor disco's lasting cultural impact.

slogans.en: Put on your dancing shoes and groove.

descriptions.en: National Eat Your Beans Day celebrates one of humanity's oldest and most nutritious foods, encouraging people to explore the huge variety of beans enjoyed around the world. Rich in fiber, protein, and minerals, beans have been a staple across nearly every culture for thousands of years. Cultivated beans date back to the seventh millennium BC—even predating pottery.

St. Thomas Day honors Thomas the Apostle, one of the twelve disciples of Jesus, remembered both as "Doubting Thomas" and as a bold missionary said to have carried Christianity as far as India. Marked on July 3rd in the Western Christian calendar, the feast is celebrated with worship and, in many communities, special traditions. It invites reflection on faith, doubt, and conviction.

National Independent Beer Run Day encourages beer lovers to support local craft breweries by stocking up on their favorite brews right before Independence Day. Founded in 2019 by the Brewers Association, it strategically lands ahead of the Fourth of July—one of the biggest beer-selling weekends of the year—to boost small breweries and connect the spirit of independence to locally made craft beer.

The International Day of Cooperatives, held on the first Saturday in July, celebrates how cooperatives improve the lives of their members and communities by blending economic success with social responsibility. The modern movement began in 1844 with English textile workers, and the International Cooperative Alliance has marked this day since 1927. The UN officially recognized it in 1992.

National Workaholics Day is a reminder to step back from excessive work and value work-life balance. It acknowledges that while hard work matters, rest, relationships, and time away from the job are essential to well-being. The term "workaholic" was coined around the 1940s, and the day highlights the body and mind's genuine need for balance.

World Circle Dance Day celebrates rhythmic, synchronized movement that connects people across the globe, integrating body, mind, heart, and spirit. Though circle dancing is an ancient practice, the modern movement began in 1970s Scotland as a way of centering retreat participants. Established in 2016, it now brings together over 250 groups from more than 25 countries.

International Kissing Day celebrates the affection expressed through kissing—romantic, familial, and friendly alike. It grew out of British National Kissing Day, established around 2005–2006, before spreading worldwide. While kissing has ancient roots noted in texts dating to 1500 BC, this modern day recognizes its role in human connection, always with respect for consent and cultural boundaries.

slogans.en: Share a kiss, spread the love.

descriptions.en: National Dive Bar Day celebrates the beloved subculture of dive bars—no-frills spots known for cheap drinks, jukeboxes, and unpretentious charm. Founded in 2018 by Seagram's Seven Crown to support historic preservation, it recognizes these neighborhood haunts as genuine cultural spaces. The July 7th date nods to the lucky number seven tied to the brand.

slogans.en: Cheap drinks, good company, no pretense.

descriptions.en: Global Forgiveness Day encourages people to let go of grudges and anger and to forgive those who have wronged them. Established in 1994 by CECA in Canada, it has grown into a worldwide observance centered on healing and reconciliation. The day reminds us that releasing resentment can free the mind and mend relationships.

The National Day of Rock 'n' Roll honors the genre's huge influence on culture and society. Rock 'n' roll didn't just shape music—it broke down social barriers and helped drive major cultural shifts, giving the world icons like Elvis Presley and The Beatles. Established by Christina Alexander in 2020, the day invites people to celebrate through listening, live performances, and sharing favorite tracks.

slogans.en: Turn it up and rock on.

names.en: National Father Daughter Take a Walk Day

descriptions.en: National Father Daughter Take a Walk Day encourages dads to spend meaningful one-on-one time with their daughters through a simple walk and shared conversation. It recognizes that daughters of every age benefit from their father's time and attention. Emerging in the 1970s as gender roles evolved, the day continues to promote strong father-daughter bonds across all stages of life.

International Peace & Love Day, founded by Ringo Starr in 2008, encourages people to spread kindness and compassion through simple, everyday acts—leading with care, not control. It began when Ringo was asked what he wanted for his birthday and replied, "peace and love." That humble wish grew into a global movement emphasizing quiet, personal choices that ripple outward into positive change.

slogans.en: Peace and love, pass it on.

descriptions.en: World Change Day is dedicated to inspiring personal and societal transformation, built on the idea that lasting change begins with each individual. Founded in Istanbul in 2017 by the International Change Federation, it had expanded to more than 100 cities by 2023. The day features everything from meditation and yoga to community gatherings and awareness initiatives.

Tell the Truth Day challenges people to spend a full day being honest in both words and actions. With research suggesting the average person tells around 200 little lies a day, the observance is a nudge toward self-awareness and integrity. It invites us to come clean about past untruths and to have more honest, open conversations.

slogans.en: Just for today, only the truth.

descriptions.en: World Allergy Day raises awareness about the growing global burden of allergic diseases and the importance of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. A joint initiative linked to the World Allergy Organization and WHO, it encourages people to learn about their allergies and manage them well. It highlights how allergies affect millions of lives and how better care can improve them.

Math 2.0 Day celebrates the powerful link between mathematics and technology, recognizing how math drives innovation across finance, engineering, and medicine. Founded in 2009 by the Math Interest Group, it reframes math not as a school chore but as a kind of superpower behind modern inventions. The day invites everyone to appreciate the numbers quietly shaping the digital world.

The Tour de France is one of the world's most prestigious cycling races, a test of human endurance across France's dramatic landscapes. Founded in 1903, the first edition covered six stages and about 2,428 km, won by Maurice Garin. Today it spans 21 stages and over 3,500 km—from flat sprints to punishing mountain climbs—captivating fans every July.

slogans.en: Endurance, glory, and the yellow jersey.

descriptions.en: The Running of the Bulls is a thrilling Spanish tradition where bulls charge through narrow streets as daring runners sprint alongside them. It traces back to the 14th century, when farmers moved bulls to market and young men began running with them to show courage. By the 16th century it became part of Pamplona's San Fermín festival, now a globally famous event held each July.

National Pitbull Awareness Month celebrates these often-misunderstood dogs and works to counter negative stereotypes. It highlights that pit bulls are loyal, affectionate companions that score remarkably well in temperament testing. First held in 2007 by the organization Bless the Bullys, it promotes responsible ownership, adoption, and a fairer reputation for the breed.

Global Energy Independence Day encourages the world to embrace alternative energy sources like solar, wind, and geothermal power. First celebrated in 2005 and founded by green-energy advocate Michael D. Antonovich, it falls on July 10th to honor inventor Nikola Tesla's birthday and his early renewable-energy vision. The day promotes reducing dependence on fossil fuels and building a sustainable future.

slogans.en: Power the future, break the dependence.

descriptions.en: Chronic Disease Awareness Day works to increase public understanding of chronic conditions and improve access to health information. Founded by the nonprofit Good Days and observed since around 2017, it educates people about prevention, early detection, and available resources. The July 10th date underscores that chronic illness drives seven of the top ten leading causes of death in the US.

World Rum Day, held on the second Saturday in July, celebrates the spirit distilled from sugarcane along with its rich heritage and global community of producers, bartenders, and fans. Founded in 2019 by Paul Jackson of the World Rum Guide, it honors rum's centuries-long story. The spirit rose to prominence in the 17th-century Caribbean and even served as currency in colonial America.

slogans.en: Raise a glass to the spirit of sugarcane.

descriptions.en: National Swimming Pool Day celebrates the simple joy of swimming and cooling off in the summer heat. It encourages people to visit local pools, splash around, and enjoy time with friends and family. First celebrated in 2016, it builds on a long history of swimming—from ancient Roman baths to the sport's modern revival after the 1896 Olympic Games.

names.en: National Cheer Up the Lonely Day

descriptions.en: National Cheer Up the Lonely Day encourages people to reach out to those feeling isolated through simple acts of kindness—a call, a visit, or a kind word. Founded by Francis Pesek of Detroit, it aims to combat the loneliness so many experience, especially those who are homebound or in care. The July 11th date marks his birthday and his lifelong spirit of compassion.

slogans.en: A small kindness can light up a day.

descriptions.en: The Fiesta de la Tirana transforms the small northern Chilean town of La Tirana into a dazzling blend of faith and culture, drawing tens of thousands to honor the Virgen del Carmen. Held around July 16th, it bursts with traditional dances, music, and elaborate costumes. Legend says it began with an indigenous princess who converted to Christianity, and Spanish missionaries later wove local traditions into Catholic devotion.

National Transplant Week, held in the first full week of July, raises awareness of the life-saving power of organ donation and encourages more people to register as donors. Established in the early 2000s with the British Transplant Society and NHS Blood and Transplant, it boosts donor sign-ups and educates the public. Its message is simple: one donor can transform many lives.

Paper Bag Day celebrates the humble, versatile paper bag and its role as an eco-friendly alternative to plastic. It honors the innovations that made it a daily essential—Charles Stilwell's 1852 bag-making machine and his 1883 square-bottom design, later improved with handles by Margaret Knight and Walter Deubener. The day encourages creative reuse and more sustainable packaging.

National Simplicity Day honors the birthday of Henry David Thoreau and celebrates the idea that living with less can bring greater happiness. It invites people to declutter their lives and minds—reading, spending time in nature, and unplugging from technology. Thoreau's two years at Walden Pond remain a timeless reminder to focus on what truly matters.

International Rock Day celebrates rocks and stones—the naturally occurring aggregates of minerals that literally form the ground beneath us. It recognizes their vital role in human history, from Stone Age tools to the metals and minerals that power modern life. The day invites curiosity about geology and the story the Earth tells through its rocks.

Embrace Your Geekness Day encourages everyone to proudly show off their passions—comics, sci-fi, gaming, tech, and every niche hobby in between. Created by Wellcat Holidays (Tom and Ruth Roy), it celebrates how being a geek has shifted from an insult to a badge of honor. The day is all about owning what you love and the creativity it sparks.

slogans.en: Own your passions, geek out proudly.

descriptions.en: International Non-Binary People's Day celebrates people whose gender identities exist beyond the traditional male/female binary. Founded in 2012 by Katje van Loon, its date sits halfway between International Women's Day and International Men's Day, symbolizing the space in between. The day aims to raise awareness, challenge discrimination, and build community for non-binary people worldwide.

The Drina Regatta is one of the region's largest water festivals, a joyful non-competitive float down Serbia's scenic Drina River from Perućac to Rogačica. Boats are decorated in vibrant colors amid music, dancing, and local food. Established in 1994 in Bajina Bašta, it honors the legacy of the river's traditional raftsmen and now draws thousands of visitors each summer.

National Clean Beauty Day celebrates cosmetics made with natural, organic ingredients that are kinder to skin and the environment. Founded in 2020 by Juice Beauty to mark its 15th anniversary, it raises awareness of the clean beauty movement and encourages safer, more sustainable choices. It reflects the idea that what we put on our skin matters as much as what we put in our bodies.

World Youth Skills Day, established by the UN General Assembly in 2015, highlights the importance of equipping young people with practical skills for work and entrepreneurship. It addresses a stark gap: youth are only about 25% of the world's population but a disproportionate share of the unemployed. The day promotes technical and vocational training as a path to opportunity.

Social Media Giving Day, launched in 2013 by Chris Sommers, turns social platforms into a force for good, inviting the world's billions of users to support causes they care about. Through donations, fundraisers, and awareness campaigns across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and X, it shows how a share or a post can help someone in need. It's a reminder that generosity scales online.

National I Love Horses Day celebrates humanity's deep, ancient bond with horses, domesticated for roughly 6,000 years. From transportation and farm work to sport and companionship, horses have shaped cultures across the world. The day honors their strength, grace, and loyalty—and invites horse lovers to spend time with these remarkable animals.

slogans.en: Grace, strength, and a loyal heart.

descriptions.en: Arctic Sea Ice Day, created by Polar Bears International, raises awareness of the rapid decline of Arctic sea ice. This vital frozen landscape sustains polar bears and marine life and helps regulate the global climate. The day calls for education and action to slow ice loss driven by a warming planet, reminding us that the far north's ice affects us all.

slogans.en: Save the ice, save the Arctic.

descriptions.en: National Respect Canada Day encourages Canadians to appreciate and honor the country's rich cultural mosaic. Established in 2014, it promotes inclusivity, unity, and mutual respect across communities. The day is a reminder to treat everyone with dignity, regardless of background, and to celebrate the diversity that shapes Canadian life.

slogans.en: Unity in diversity, respect for all.

descriptions.en: National Give Something Away Day encourages people to practice generosity by donating items, time, or kindness to those in need. Founded in 2015 by Linda Eaton Hall-Fulcher as a grassroots effort, it highlights how giving benefits both the receiver and the giver, including a boost to well-being. It's a simple prompt to declutter with purpose and spread a little good.

slogans.en: Give a little, brighten a lot.

descriptions.en: Saint Swithin's Day commemorates a humble 9th-century Bishop of Winchester known for his charity. English folklore holds that the weather on this day sets the pattern for the next 40 days: "St Swithin's day if thou dost rain, for forty days it will remain." The tradition blends faith, legend, and a bit of meteorological superstition into an enduring English custom.

Celebration of the Horse Day honors the deep bond between people and horses—built on trust, steady movement, and quiet understanding—and their role in healing, teaching, and bringing communities together. While the U.S. Senate established a December National Day of the Horse in 2004, this informal summer celebration grew organically to let people gather outdoors and honor horses through learning and connection.

National Cherry Day celebrates the sweet, jewel-red fruit of summer, enjoyed fresh, baked, or preserved. It encourages cherry picking, festivals, and baking, from pies to preserves. Cherries originated in Asia Minor, were spread by the Greeks and Romans, and reached America with English colonists in the 1600s.

slogans.en: Life is just a bowl of cherries.

descriptions.en: National Personal Chef Day honors the culinary pros who cook for individuals, families, and businesses — and the home cooks who feed their loved ones too. Founded by the United States Personal Chef Association, it recognizes the skill and care behind everyday meals. It's a nod to anyone who turns ingredients into something nourishing and memorable.

Artificial Intelligence Appreciation Day celebrates how AI quietly improves daily life — from navigation and smart assistants to healthcare diagnostics — while stressing fair, ethical, and responsible design. Founded in 2021 by A.I. Heart LLC, it invites open conversations about AI's real-world impact and its future role in society.

The World Day for International Justice highlights the global fight against war crimes, genocide, and crimes against humanity, and the pursuit of accountability for victims. It marks the adoption of the Rome Statute in 1998, which created the International Criminal Court as a permanent institution. The day promotes justice, human rights, and the rule of law worldwide.

National Tattoo Day celebrates the rich history and artistry of tattoos as forms of self-expression. Tattoos have ancient roots — Ötzi the Iceman bore them 5,000 years ago — and appear across cultures from Egypt and China to Polynesia. The day honors that heritage, celebrates modern tattoo artists, and challenges lingering stigma around body art.

slogans.en: Ink your story on your skin.

descriptions.en: The International Snowdon Race is a punishing mountain run up and down Snowdon (Yr Wyddfa), Wales's highest peak, over a 15.35 km course from Llanberis. Held on the third Saturday in July, it draws elite fell runners from around the world. It began in 1976 when Ken Jones wondered how fast someone could run up and down the mountain — 86 runners took the first challenge.

slogans.en: Up the mountain and back — if you can.

descriptions.en: World Listening Day invites us to truly listen to the world around us — its soundscapes, its acoustic ecology, its quiet and its clamor — not just to one another. Rooted in the World Soundscape Project and first held in 2010, it falls on the birthday of composer R. Murray Schafer, a founder of acoustic ecology. It's a call to notice, and protect, the sounds of our environment.

slogans.en: Listen to the world around you.

descriptions.en: Perfect Family Day celebrates family bonds through simple, meaningful time together — a shared meal, a game, an outdoor adventure. Established in 1999, it grew from a wish to help people slow down and reconnect. Its message is gentle and inclusive: whatever your family looks like, time spent together is what makes it perfect.

Moon Day celebrates humanity's first lunar landing on July 20, 1969, when Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon during Apollo 11. It honors one of history's greatest feats of exploration and engineering. Established in the US in 1971 and designated International Moon Day by the UN in 2021, it reflects on our ongoing journey into space.

slogans.en: One small step, one giant leap.

descriptions.en: Friend's Day (Día del Amigo) is a beloved Argentine celebration of friendship, when people fill cafés and homes to toast the bonds they share. It was inspired by the 1969 Apollo 11 Moon landing — dentist Enrique Febbraro saw humanity's shared achievement as proof friendship could unite the world. Officially recognized in 1979, it's now one of Argentina's most social days.

slogans.en: Here's to friends, near and far.

descriptions.en: National Lollipop Day celebrates the cheerful candy on a stick that has brightened childhoods for generations. While ancient Egyptians and Chinese preserved fruit and nuts on sticks, the modern lollipop emerged in the late 1800s, and the Bradley Smith Company patented the name in 1932. The day is a sweet invitation to enjoy one and share the joy.

slogans.en: Sweeten your day, one lick at a time.

descriptions.en: World Jump Day is a playful, tongue-in-cheek event inviting people worldwide to jump at the same moment — originally an art project claiming a synchronized leap could nudge Earth's orbit and fight climate change. It's physically impossible, of course, but that's the point: a witty celebration of collective action and global connection. Created by artist Torsten Lauschmann, first held in 2006.

Global Hug Your Kids Day encourages parents to hug their children and cherish the time they have together. Founded in 2008 by Michelle Nichols — a decade after she lost her young son to cancer — it's a tender reminder that childhood passes quickly. It also celebrates the real health benefits of hugs, from lower stress to a stronger heart.

slogans.en: Hug them tight while they're small.

descriptions.en: Gentse Feesten is one of Europe's largest cultural festivals — ten days of music, theatre, street performance, and food filling the historic heart of Ghent, Belgium. It began in 1843 as a city-organized community celebration and grew over generations into a massive, joyful summer institution. Despite wartime interruptions, it has always returned stronger.

slogans.en: Ten days of music, joy, and Ghent.

descriptions.en: No Pet Store Puppies Day raises awareness of puppy mills and urges people to adopt from shelters instead of buying from pet stores. Many pet-shop puppies come from large breeding facilities that put profit over welfare, keeping dogs in cramped, unhealthy conditions. Launched by the ASPCA in 2011, it champions #AdoptDontShop and humane treatment of animals.

World Collie Day celebrates one of the most intelligent and devoted dog breeds, known for alert eyes, flowing coats, and a calm, loyal nature. Collies originated as herding dogs in Scotland and northern England, rose to fame after Queen Victoria adopted the breed, and became icons through Lassie. The day honors their loyalty and the deep bonds they form with people.

Pi Approximation Day celebrates the fraction 22/7, a handy estimate of π (about 3.1429) — hence the date 22/7. A summery, lighter cousin of Pi Day (March 14), it's popular in schools and science centers, with games, food, and puzzles. The approximation dates back over 2,000 years to Archimedes, who used it to bound the value of pi.

names.en: National Women Touched by Addiction Day

descriptions.en: National Women Touched by Addiction Day honors women who have faced addiction themselves or supported loved ones through recovery. It works to reduce stigma, share stories of resilience, and create compassionate space for healing. Founded in 2021 by Mending Hearts, a Nashville nonprofit, it grew from their mission to house and support women in recovery.

Tisha B'Av is a solemn Jewish day of mourning and fasting, remembering the destruction of both Temples in Jerusalem and other tragedies in Jewish history. Observed on the 9th of Av (July 22–23 in 2026), it involves fasting, reading the Book of Lamentations, and quiet reflection. Its roots stretch back over 2,500 years to the fall of the First Temple in 586 BCE.

slogans.en: A day of mourning and remembrance.

descriptions.en: The Galway International Arts Festival transforms the Irish city into a two-week hub of theatre, music, dance, and visual art each July, drawing hundreds of thousands of visitors. Performances spill from theatres into public squares and streets. Founded in 1978 by artists including Ollie Jennings and Bill Whelan, it has grown into one of Europe's leading arts events.

slogans.en: Two weeks of art fills Galway.

descriptions.en: The Festival of Archaeology invites people across the UK to explore the nation's heritage through digs, tours, workshops, and talks, making the distant past feel vivid and hands-on. It runs for a fortnight each July to coincide with peak fieldwork season. Organised by the Council for British Archaeology, it began in 1990 as National Archaeology Day with just ten activities.

National Tequila Day toasts the iconic Mexican spirit distilled from blue agave, the star of margaritas and countless cocktails. Tequila's roots run deep — its ancestor pulque was made as early as 150 BC — and true tequila must be at least 51% blue agave from regions like Jalisco. Mexico officially recognized the day in 2018 as a global celebration.

slogans.en: Salt, lime, and a taste of Mexico.

descriptions.en: Pioneer Day is a Utah state holiday marking the arrival of Brigham Young and the first Latter-day Saint pioneers in the Salt Lake Valley on July 24, 1847. It celebrates their westward journey, resilience, and the communities they built. Utahns mark it with parades, rodeos, fireworks, and family gatherings honoring the pioneers' legacy.

National Wine and Cheese Day, celebrated on July 25, honors one of the world's most beloved culinary pairings. The combination of wine and cheese dates back thousands of years, both products sharing a reliance on the science of fermentation and aging. Across the globe, enthusiasts gather for tastings and pairings that highlight regional varieties of wine and artisanal cheeses. Whether a bold red with aged cheddar or a crisp white with brie, this day invites everyone to explore the art of pairing.

National Day of the Cowboy is celebrated on the fourth Saturday of July in the United States, honoring the enduring legacy of the American cowboy. Cowboys played a central role in the development of the American West, herding cattle across vast open ranges and shaping the culture of frontier life. Today the day is marked by rodeos, western festivals, and celebrations of cowboy culture including music, art, and horsemanship. The cowboy spirit of independence, hard work, and freedom continues to inspire people around the world.

Carousel Day celebrates the timeless magic of the carousel, one of the oldest and most beloved amusement rides in history. The modern carousel traces its origins to 17th-century Europe, evolving from equestrian training devices into the ornate spinning rides adorned with hand-carved horses and fantasy animals we know today. On July 25, 1871, the first US patent for a steam-powered carousel was granted, making this date its official anniversary. Carousels continue to delight riders of all ages at amusement parks, boardwalks, and town squares around the world.

slogans.en: Round and round, the magic never stops.

descriptions.en: The Feast of Saint James, celebrated on July 25, honors James the Great, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus and the patron saint of Spain. According to tradition, James was the first apostle to be martyred, beheaded by Herod Agrippa around 44 AD, and his relics are believed to rest at the Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela in Spain. The feast is especially significant in Galicia, where Santiago de Compostela serves as the destination of the famous Camino pilgrimage route. Thousands of pilgrims complete the Camino each year, arriving at the cathedral to pay their respects on this holy day.

slogans.en: The way of Saint James leads to grace.

names.en: International Day of Women and Girls of African Descent

descriptions.en: The International Day of Women and Girls of African Descent, observed on July 25, was proclaimed by the United Nations in 2021 to recognize and address the unique forms of discrimination faced by women and girls of African descent worldwide. These women and girls are disproportionately affected by intersecting forms of racism, sexism, and poverty. The day calls on governments and civil society to take concrete steps to eliminate racial discrimination and promote gender equality. It amplifies the voices of African-descendant women in politics, culture, science, and the arts.

slogans.en: Their voices rise, their strength endures.

descriptions.en: National Marine Week, observed in late July in the United Kingdom, is an annual celebration organized by The Wildlife Trusts to highlight the rich biodiversity of Britain's seas and coastlines. The event encourages people to discover, explore, and protect the marine environment through rockpooling, guided snorkeling, and beach clean-ups. Britain's seas are home to thousands of species, from seals and dolphins to colorful anemones and starfish. The week raises awareness of the threats facing ocean habitats, including plastic pollution, climate change, and overfishing.

slogans.en: Dive into the blue — our seas need you.

descriptions.en: National Dog Photography Day, celebrated on July 26, is a day for dog lovers and photography enthusiasts to capture their furry friends in all their playful, goofy, and adorable glory. Dogs are among the most photogenic subjects in the world, their expressions and antics making for endlessly joyful images. The day encourages pet owners to pick up their cameras — or smartphones — and document their dogs' unique personalities and favorite moments. From action shots in the park to cozy portraits at home, this day celebrates the unbreakable bond between humans and their canine companions.

Esperanto Day, observed on July 26, commemorates the publication of the first Esperanto textbook on July 26, 1887, by Dr. Ludwik Lazarus Zamenhof. Zamenhof, a Polish ophthalmologist, created Esperanto as a neutral international language intended to foster peace and understanding among people of different nations. Today, Esperanto is spoken by an estimated one to two million people worldwide, making it the most widely spoken constructed language. The day celebrates the enduring vision of a world united by a shared language, free from the barriers that divide us.

names.en: World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly

descriptions.en: The World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly, held on the fourth Sunday of July, was instituted by Pope Francis in 2021 to honor the role of grandparents and elderly people in the life of families and society. The day encourages younger generations to visit and spend time with their grandparents and elderly relatives, combating the epidemic of loneliness that affects many older people. Elderly people carry irreplaceable wisdom, memories, and love that form the foundation of families and communities. The annual theme always centers on the dignity, presence, and invaluable contribution of the elderly.

Love Parks Week, held in late July in the United Kingdom, is an annual campaign celebrating the importance of public parks and green spaces in communities across Britain. Organized by Keep Britain Tidy and other conservation groups, the week encourages people to get outside, enjoy their local parks, and take pride in caring for these shared spaces. Parks play a crucial role in public health and wellbeing, offering free recreational space, nature connection, and community gathering points. Activities include litter picks, nature walks, picnics, and community events that bring neighborhoods together.

slogans.en: Love your park, love your community.

descriptions.en: National Fishing Month, celebrated throughout August in the United Kingdom, is an annual initiative that encourages people of all ages to try fishing for the first time or rediscover the sport. Fishing is one of Britain's most popular leisure activities, with millions of anglers enjoying rivers, lakes, canals, and coastal waters each year. The campaign provides free or subsidized fishing sessions to introduce newcomers to the sport, emphasizing the mental health benefits of time spent quietly by the water. The month celebrates fishing as a pursuit that connects people to nature, builds patience, and fosters a love of the outdoors.

slogans.en: Cast a line, catch a memory.

descriptions.en: National Tree Day, celebrated on the first Sunday of August in Australia, is the country's largest community tree-planting event. Founded in 1996 by Planet Ark, the initiative has seen more than 24 million trees and plants planted by over four million Australians at schools, parks, bushland reserves, and local community spaces. Planting trees is a simple but powerful act for fighting climate change, restoring habitats, and improving local environments. National Tree Day inspires Australians to connect with nature and take tangible action to protect the natural world for future generations.

slogans.en: Plant a tree, grow a future.

descriptions.en: National Scotch Day celebrates Scotland's centuries-old whisky tradition, honoring the distilling craft passed down since medieval monks first brought spirit-making techniques to the Highlands. What began as a medicinal tonic evolved into the aged, peated spirit prized by drinkers worldwide today. The day invites enthusiasts to sample single malts and blends from Scotland's many storied distilleries.

slogans.en: Raise a glass to Scotland's finest.

descriptions.en: Sleepy Head Day is a centuries-old Finnish tradition that pokes affectionate fun at the last person in the household to wake up. Rooted in medieval legend and moved from June to July in 1709, the custom says late risers will be sluggish for the rest of the year. Families mark it playfully with a splash of water, while the town of Naantali holds a famous public ceremony tossing a celebrity into the sea.

names.en: National Korean War Veterans Armistice Day

descriptions.en: This observance honors the Americans who served in the Korean War, which began on June 25, 1950, when North Korean forces invaded the South. After three years of brutal fighting, an armistice was signed on July 27, 1953, halting active combat and creating the Korean Demilitarized Zone that still divides the peninsula. Often called the "Forgotten War," the day ensures its veterans and their sacrifices are remembered.

names.en: International Safe Places to Work Day

descriptions.en: International Safe Places to Work Day shines a spotlight on workplaces where people feel free to speak up, question, disagree, and be themselves without fear. Founded by the Safe Places to Work initiative, it champions psychological safety alongside physical safety, drawing on research like Google's Project Aristotle, which found that teams perform best when members feel safe to be vulnerable. The day encourages leaders to build trust and openness into everyday culture.

National Milk Chocolate Day celebrates the creamy confection made from cocoa solids blended with dry or condensed milk. Swiss inventor Daniel Peter developed it in the 1870s after his neighbor Henri Nestlé's milk-powder process inspired him to soften dark chocolate's bitterness. His innovation sparked a sweeter alternative that would go on to dominate the global chocolate market. Today, the day is marked with a well-earned bar — or ten.

National Lipstick Day celebrates one of beauty's most iconic products and its centuries-long history of self-expression. Founded by beauty entrepreneur Huda Kattan in 2016, the day invites people to experiment with bold new shades and celebrate the confidence a swipe of color can bring. From ancient natural pigments to today's endless finishes and formulas, lipstick remains a small, powerful act of personal style.

National Lasagna Day pays tribute to the layered Italian pasta dish that has become a beloved staple in kitchens around the world. Tracing its origins to medieval Naples, lasagna made its way to America in the 19th century and has since taken on countless regional twists — from classic beef and béchamel to vegetarian and seafood variations. The day is best celebrated with a generously layered, bubbling tray straight from the oven.

Rain Day celebrates the quiet, life-giving importance of rainfall to every living thing on Earth. The tradition began in the late 1800s when pharmacist William Allison noticed it rained on July 29 in Waynesburg, Pennsylvania almost every year, a curious pattern that gained worldwide attention in the 1930s thanks to journalist John O'Hara. Today people mark it by learning about rainfall patterns, dancing in a summer shower, or simply appreciating water's role in sustaining life.

slogans.en: Let it pour, let it matter.

descriptions.en: National Cheesecake Day celebrates one of the world's oldest and most beloved desserts, believed to have been invented by the Ancient Greeks around 200 A.D. as one of the first-ever "sweet" treats. First conceived in 1985, the observance took off with the rise of the internet in the early 2000s and is now marked worldwide. People celebrate with everything from classic New York-style slices to fruit-topped, no-bake, and chocolate-swirled variations.

Pol'and'Rock Festival, formerly known as Woodstock Festival Poland, began in 1995 as a free tribute concert honoring volunteers of the Great Orchestra of Christmas Charity. It has since grown into one of Europe's largest non-commercial music festivals, drawing hundreds of thousands of fans to the Polish countryside for days of live music, workshops, and social activism. Founded by Jerzy Owsiak, the festival remains free to all, championing peace, unity, and inclusivity.

National Mutt Day, also marked again each December 2, celebrates mixed-breed dogs and raises awareness of the many wonderful mutts still waiting in shelters. Founded by animal welfare advocate Colleen Paige, the day pushes back against the stigma sometimes attached to the word "mutt," highlighting how these dogs often combine the best traits of multiple breeds. It's a call to adopt, care for, and celebrate every one-of-a-kind mixed-breed companion.

The Flower Fair, known locally as Feria de las Flores, transforms Medellín into a vibrant celebration of floral artistry and Colombian pride. Founded in 1957 by tourism promoter Arturo Uribe as a modest five-day festival with 40 silleteros (flower-carrying farmers), it has grown into a ten-day celebration drawing visitors from around the world. The signature Silleteros Parade sees locals carry towering, elaborate flower arrangements on their backs, alongside music, dance, and food honoring the region's growers.

National Girlfriends Day celebrates the deep bonds between female friends, honoring both lifelong companions and newer connections. It's a day to reach out, reconnect, and show appreciation for the women who provide unwavering support and laughter.

slogans.en: Celebrate the women who have your back.

descriptions.en: National Spider-Man Day honors the iconic web-slinging superhero created by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko in 1962. Fans mark the day with comics, films, and memorabilia celebrating six decades of the friendly neighborhood hero.

slogans.en: With great power comes a great celebration.

descriptions.en: World Lung Cancer Day raises awareness of one of the most common and deadliest cancers worldwide. The day highlights research, prevention, and early detection efforts to reduce the disease's toll.

International Blues Music Day celebrates the blues, a genre born from African American communities in the American South that gave voice to resilience, pain, and joy. The day honors blues musicians and preserves this influential musical tradition worldwide.

International Childfree Day celebrates people who have chosen not to have children, recognizing that fulfillment and purpose can be found in many paths of life. It challenges stereotypes and honors the diversity of modern lifestyles.
Respect for Parents Day encourages people of all ages to express gratitude toward their parents for their guidance and support. It's a reminder that respect between generations begins at home.
National Yorkie Day celebrates the Yorkshire Terrier, a tiny dog breed known for its big personality. Owners mark the day with grooming, playdates, and support for Yorkie rescue organizations.
Albariño Day celebrates the crisp, aromatic white wine grape grown mainly in Spain's Rías Baixas region. Wine lovers around the world uncork a bottle to toast this refreshing summer varietal.

National Sunflower Day celebrates the bright, towering flower that blooms throughout summer. The day encourages people to visit sunflower fields, plant their own, and share the joy this cheerful bloom brings.

slogans.en: Turn your face to the sun.

descriptions.en: Sandcastle Day invites people to head to a beach, lake, or sandbox and build the greatest sandcastle they can imagine. It's a celebration of creativity and the simple, nostalgic joy of playing in the sand.

National Ice Cream Sandwich Day celebrates the classic frozen treat of ice cream pressed between two cookies or wafers. Enjoyed since street vendors sold them in 1800s New York, it remains one of America's favorite frozen novelties.

slogans.en: Two cookies, one scoop of joy.

descriptions.en: National Sisters Day honors the unique bond between sisters, celebrating the support, laughter, and shared history they carry through life. It's a day to reconnect and show appreciation for that irreplaceable relationship.

slogans.en: The bond that knows you best.

descriptions.en: National Friendship Day gives people a chance to show appreciation and affection toward their friends. Distinct from the UN's global International Day of Friendship in July, this US observance encourages quality time, cards, and thoughtful gestures.

Psychic Day invites people to explore their intuitive side through playful games like guessing a caller's identity or predicting a card's color. With roots in 19th-century England, the tradition was formalized as National Psychic Week in the 1960s.

International Assistance Dog Week celebrates the hardworking dogs that support people with disabilities, from guiding the blind to alerting for medical conditions. The week also honors the trainers and organizations that prepare these dogs for their vital roles.
National Watermelon Day celebrates the juicy summer favorite that's 92% water, perfect for smoothies, salads, or a slice on a hot day.
Festival Monday is a late-summer public holiday marked by outdoor festivals, music, and parades before autumn begins.
Commerce Day celebrates the role trade and business play in everyday life, honoring the merchants and workers who keep communities and economies moving.
Natal Day marks the founding of Nova Scotia, celebrated with community festivities, parades, and fireworks that bring locals and visitors together.
National Chocolate Chip Cookie Day honors the classic treat first baked by Ruth Wakefield in the 1930s and celebrates its rise into an iconic American dessert enjoyed worldwide.

slogans.en: A timeless treat, one chip at a time.

descriptions.en: National Night Out strengthens community-police partnerships through neighborhood gatherings, cookouts, and safety events held since 1984.
National White Wine Day invites enthusiasts to explore crisp varietals and history, gathering with friends to enjoy white wine pairings.
Single Working Women's Day recognizes the hard work, independence, and unique challenges of single working women, celebrating their contributions to society and the economy.
International Clouded Leopard Day raises awareness for this vulnerable big cat species, whose population is rapidly declining due to habitat loss and poaching.
Assistance Dog Day celebrates the incredible support assistance dogs provide to people with disabilities and special needs, from guiding the blind to alerting for medical conditions.
National Peach Month, established by President Ronald Reagan, celebrates this juicy summer fruit and encourages people to enjoy peaches all August long.
Blogger Day celebrates blogging as a medium for self-expression and connection, honoring writers who share everything from personal stories to professional expertise online.
National Underwear Day promotes body positivity and self-acceptance, encouraging people to embrace their favorite undergarments and body image with confidence.

names.en: National Work Like A Dog Day

descriptions.en: National Work Like A Dog Day encourages grit and determination at work, inspired by the tireless work ethic of dogs, and celebrates those who consistently give their all.
Professional Engineers Day honors licensed engineers and their contributions to industry, infrastructure, and the economy, established in 2016 by the National Society of Professional Engineers.

slogans.en: Building the world, one design at a time.

descriptions.en: National Opportunity Day encourages students and career-changers to explore unconventional paths, highlighting alternative routes beyond the traditional education-to-career track.

slogans.en: Every path can lead somewhere great.

descriptions.en: Stop on Red Week raises awareness about the dangers of running red lights, promoting safer driving habits to protect pedestrians, cyclists, and other road users.
International Scuba Day celebrates underwater diving and marine exploration, uniting divers worldwide and promoting awareness of ocean conservation.

slogans.en: Dive into a whole new world.

descriptions.en: Balloons to Heaven Day honors lives lost to gun violence, using symbolic gestures like releasing balloons to express grief and support collective healing.
Jamaica Independence Day commemorates August 6, 1962, when Jamaica gained independence from British rule, celebrated nationwide with parades, music, and cultural pride.
International Beer Day celebrates the craft of brewing, bringing friends together to enjoy a cold beer while honoring brewers and bartenders worldwide.
Aged Care Employee Day celebrates the diverse workforce behind aged care — from kitchen staff to cleaners — recognizing everyone who helps elderly residents feel comfortable and connected.

slogans.en: The quiet heroes of aged care.

descriptions.en: Scottish Wildcat Day raises awareness for Scotland's critically endangered 'Highland tiger,' threatened by habitat loss, disease, and hybridization with domestic cats.
National Happiness Happens Day encourages people to share their joy with others and focus on positive moments rather than negativity.

slogans.en: Share the joy, spread the happiness.

descriptions.en: National Dollar Day commemorates the Continental Congress establishing the dollar as the United States' currency in 1786, celebrating this iconic banknote's history.

slogans.en: A currency, a history, a legacy.

descriptions.en: Digital Nomad Day celebrates remote workers who blend careers with global exploration, swapping offices for cafes, coworking spaces, and beachside tables.
International Hangover Day humorously acknowledges the morning-after effects of a big night out, pairing with International Beer Day the day before.
International Infinity Day invites reflection on endless possibilities, exploring infinity through philosophy, art, science, and creative expression.

Melon Day celebrates Turkmenistan's prized melon harvest, especially the fragrant Turkmenbashi variety cherished across Central Asia. Markets and squares fill with towering melon displays, tastings, and festive parades honoring the fruit's place in Turkmen culture.

slogans.en: A taste of paradise, one slice at a time.

descriptions.en: Betty Boop Day celebrates the iconic animated flapper who first appeared on screen in 1930 and became a symbol of independence and style. Fans mark the day with classic cartoon marathons, retro parties, and jazz-age nostalgia.

International Coworking Day celebrates the shared-workspace movement born in San Francisco in 2005, honoring how coworking spaces connect freelancers, remote workers, and entrepreneurs. It highlights the collaboration, flexibility, and community that flow from working independently, together.

Hold Hands Day celebrates one of the simplest, most powerful gestures of human connection. People are encouraged to hold hands with loved ones, friends, or family as a quiet expression of affection, comfort, and support.

slogans.en: A little touch, a lot of love.

descriptions.en: South Africa's National Women's Day commemorates the 1956 march when over 20,000 women walked to the Union Buildings in Pretoria to protest apartheid pass laws. The day honors women's role in the struggle for equality and continues to advocate for gender justice.

Europe's largest hot air balloon event fills the skies above Bristol's Ashton Court with hundreds of balloons for dawn and dusk ascents. Founded in 1979 with just 27 balloons, the festival now draws huge crowds for its illuminated night-glow display, music, and fairground attractions.

Vlogging Day celebrates video bloggers and the global community they've built through online storytelling. Established in 2018 by the UK video festival Summer in the City, it encourages both seasoned creators and newcomers to pick up a camera and share their voice.

National Lazy Day gives everyone permission to slow down and do absolutely nothing. Whether it's sleeping in, binge-watching TV, or lounging around guilt-free, the day celebrates the restorative power of a little downtime.

Japan Mountain Day (Yama-no-Hi) invites people to appreciate mountains and the blessings they provide. Established as a national holiday in 2016 after a grassroots campaign, the date was chosen because the number 8 resembles a mountain and 11 resembles two trees.

Play in the Sand Day is an invitation to kick off your shoes and get creative at the beach, lake shore, or backyard sandbox. From sandcastles to treasure hunts, the day celebrates the simple, tactile joy of digging in and letting imagination run free.

Ekka People's Day is a beloved public holiday in Brisbane held during the Royal Queensland Show, bringing city and country together. The Brisbane Showgrounds fill with agricultural displays, livestock competitions, sideshow rides, and local food stalls celebrating Queensland's rural heritage.

Thailand marks the birthday of Queen Sirikit, revered as the Mother of the Nation, as its national Mother's Day. Streets fill with blue decorations and portraits, while families gather for jasmine garland ceremonies where children honor their mothers with songs and gratitude.

slogans.en: Honoring the Mother of the Nation.

descriptions.en: World Lizard Day celebrates the roughly 7,000 lizard species found across the planet, from tiny geckos to giant monitors. Schools, zoos, and reptile fans use the day to learn about lizards' remarkable adaptations, habitats, and ecological importance.

Financial Awareness Day highlights money management as an essential life skill, from budgeting and saving to planning ahead. The day encourages people at every income level to build confidence through financial knowledge and consistent habits rather than relying on chance.

slogans.en: Know your money, own your future.

descriptions.en: Southeast Europe's largest film event transforms Sarajevo into a hub for filmmakers and movie lovers each August. Founded in 1995 during the Bosnian War to bring culture and hope to the besieged city, the festival now honors cinematic excellence with its prestigious Heart of Sarajevo awards.

National Relaxation Day is dedicated to unwinding and stepping away from work and chores for a while. Founded in 1985 by nine-year-old Sean Moeller, the day reminds everyone that taking a break is essential for preventing burnout and recharging.

The Nile Festival honors the river that has sustained life and civilization in Egypt for millennia. Tracing back to ancient ceremonies celebrating the annual flood that brought fertile soil, the modern festival fills riverbank communities with color, music, and gratitude.

World Greatness Day celebrates greatness in everyday people, not just fame or major achievements. Created in 2019 by Professor Patrick Businge, it invites reflection on small victories, daily kindness, and the quiet strength that lifts others up.

Navasard is the ancient Armenian New Year, once marked with music, dance, communal feasts, and athletic games honoring the harvest and the gods. Dating back thousands of years to pre-Christian Armenia, the celebration has been kept alive in modern cultural revivals.

slogans.en: An ancient new year, still alive.

descriptions.en: National Science Week fills Australia with over a thousand events, from hands-on experiments to public lectures, inspiring people of all ages to engage with science. Launched in 1997, it celebrates researchers' contributions and sparks curiosity in the next generation.

Every two years, Brussels' Grand Place transforms into a breathtaking carpet of hundreds of thousands of begonias, arranged in an intricate new design each edition. Created in 1971 by landscape architect E. Stautemans, the biennial display celebrates Belgium's horticultural artistry at the UNESCO World Heritage square.

National Rum Day toasts the Caribbean spirit's centuries-old legacy, from its 17th-century origins as a fermented byproduct of sugar refining to its status as one of the world's most beloved drinks. Bars and distilleries worldwide mark the day with rum cocktails, tastings, and tributes to the U.S. Virgin Islands, where the observance began.

slogans.en: Raise a glass, it's Rum Day!

descriptions.en: National Black Cat Appreciation Day celebrates black cats and pushes back against centuries-old superstitions that unfairly branded them as unlucky. The day highlights how differently black cats are viewed around the world — as symbols of good fortune in Japan and parts of Britain, and simply as loyal companions everywhere else.

slogans.en: Black cats bring good luck too.

descriptions.en: National Nonprofit Day honors the charitable organizations that power education, healthcare, and social justice work across the country. The date marks the anniversary of the Tariff Act of 1894, which first granted U.S. nonprofits tax-exempt status, paving the way for the modern nonprofit sector.

Nag Panchami is a Hindu festival honoring Naga serpent deities, observed on the fifth day of the bright half of the lunar month of Shravana. Devotees offer prayers and milk to serpent idols or live snakes, seeking protection and blessings, in a tradition rooted in ancient reverence for nature during the monsoon season.

National Couple's Day gives partners a reason to celebrate their relationship outside of Valentine's Day, roughly six months later on the calendar. Rather than obligatory gifts, the day encourages quality time, small gestures of appreciation, and genuine connection between couples.

Serendipity Day celebrates the happy accidents and unexpected good fortune that shape our lives. Inspired by the 18th-century coinage of the word 'serendipity' from the Persian fairy tale 'The Three Princes of Serendip,' the day encourages people to stay open to chance encounters and pleasant surprises.

Never Give Up Day celebrates resilience and determination in the face of setbacks. The observance encourages people to keep pushing toward their goals, surround themselves with supportive people, and recognize that persistence — even in small daily steps — is what ultimately gets you there.

Solidarity Day in Chile began in 1978 when Cardinal Raúl Silva Henríquez launched a nationwide drive to collect food, clothing, and essentials for struggling families. Nearly five decades later, it remains a cherished tradition that unites Chileans in collective compassion and support for those facing hardship.

International Delivery Driver Appreciation Day thanks the couriers who keep food and packages moving through busy city streets, rain or shine. Launched in 2023, the date plays on '8-18' resembling a rider with a delivery pack, a fitting tribute to the fast-paced work delivery drivers do every day.

National Aviation Day was established in 1939 by President Franklin D. Roosevelt to honor the birthday of Orville Wright and celebrate the impact of flight. The day recognizes the Wright brothers' pioneering achievements and decades of aviation progress that transformed how the world travels.

slogans.en: Look up — the sky's the limit.

descriptions.en: National Potato Day celebrates the humble tuber that has quietly shaped world history, agriculture, and cuisine since its domestication in the Andes thousands of years ago. Now the world's fifth most-cultivated crop, the potato gets its due with mashed, roasted, and fried tributes around the globe.

National Finance Brokers Day recognizes the mortgage and finance brokers who help everyday people navigate loans and financial decisions. Founded in Australia in 2015, the day has grown into an international celebration marked by conferences, education initiatives, and appreciation for brokers around the world.

National Radio Day celebrates the enduring medium that has connected communities since Heinrich Hertz's discovery of radio waves and Guglielmo Marconi's early transmissions. The date recalls Detroit's 8MK station's first broadcast in 1920, honoring radio's continuing role in music, news, and companionship.

slogans.en: Tune in and turn it up.

descriptions.en: Bullying. No Way! Week unites Australian schools, students, and families in tackling bullying together. Thousands of schools take part in activities that help young people recognize bullying, understand its impact, and take positive action to build safer, more inclusive communities.

names.en: International Day of Remembrance and Tribute to the Victims of Terrorism

descriptions.en: The UN General Assembly established this day in 2017 to honor victims and survivors of terrorism and raise awareness of the need for international solidarity against violent extremism. The observance also highlights support for women, children, and survivors of terrorism-related gender-based violence.

National Senior Citizens Day, proclaimed by President Ronald Reagan in 1988, honors the wisdom, achievements, and contributions of older generations. The day encourages spending time with seniors, listening to their stories, and helping combat the isolation that can come with aging.

The Gold Cup Parade has filled the streets of Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island, with floats, marching bands, antique cars, and giant balloons since 1962. What began as a bid to revive Old Home Week has grown into the largest parade in Atlantic Canada.

National Eat A Peach Day celebrates the juicy stone fruit that traveled from its origins in northwest China to orchards around the world. Whether eaten fresh, baked into a cobbler, or blended into a summer dessert, a perfectly ripe peach is a small, sweet reason to celebrate.

Ride the Wind Day marks the day in 1977 the human-powered Gossamer Condor won the Kremer Prize with the first sustained, controlled flight. It celebrates the freedom of flight and every wind-powered joy, from kites and windsurfing to simply chasing a breeze.

slogans.en: Catch the breeze, chase the sky.

descriptions.en: Created in 2021 by Sarah Horne after her dog Shammy lost his sight, International Blind Dog Day challenges the myth that blind dogs can't live full, happy lives. It celebrates their resilience and encourages adoption, showing that a little extra care goes a long way.

Established by President Franklin D. Roosevelt in the 1930s to coincide with Orville Wright's birthday, National Aviation Week honors the pioneers and breakthroughs of flight. It celebrates how aviation connected the world and inspires the next generation of pilots, engineers and dreamers.

Vesuvius Day remembers the catastrophic eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD, which buried the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash and preserved them for centuries. It's a day to reflect on nature's power and the remarkable history frozen in time beneath the volcano.

Started in 1997 by New York musician Patrick Grant, International Strange Music Day invites everyone to listen without prejudice and explore sounds far outside their usual playlist. Play something unfamiliar, discover a weird new genre, and let curiosity lead your ears.

On August 24, 2006, the International Astronomical Union redefined what makes a planet and reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet. The controversial decision shrank the solar system to eight planets and still sparks friendly debate among stargazers everywhere.

slogans.en: Still a planet in our hearts.

descriptions.en: Kiss and Make Up Day is a gentle nudge to mend fences, let go of grudges, and reconnect with the people who matter. Reach out with a sincere apology or a warm hug — because making up is the best part of any argument.

slogans.en: Let it go, make it right.

descriptions.en: National Secondhand Wardrobe Day champions the joy of thrifting and pre-loved fashion. By giving clothes a second life, we cut waste, save resources and find one-of-a-kind style — proving that sustainable can be seriously stylish.

Women's Equality Day commemorates August 26, 1920, when the 19th Amendment gave American women the right to vote. First observed in 1973, it honors the long fight for suffrage and renews the call for full equality in every part of life.

Mawlid al-Nabi marks the birth of the Prophet Muhammad and is observed by Muslims around the world. Falling on the 12th of Rabi al-Awwal in the Islamic calendar, it is a time for prayer, poetry, charity and community gatherings that reflect on his teachings of compassion.

Belgian Beer Week raises a glass to Belgium's legendary brewing heritage, from Trappist ales and lambics to bold modern craft. Launched by the Belgian Brewers, it invites enthusiasts everywhere to savour the craftsmanship and centuries of tradition in every pour.

National Burger Day is a mouth-watering tribute to one of the world's favourite comfort foods. From classic beef stacks to gourmet and plant-based creations, it's the perfect excuse to fire up the grill and build your dream burger.

slogans.en: Stack it high, bite it deep.

descriptions.en: International Lottery Day celebrates the age-old thrill of trying your luck. Lotteries have funded public works and good causes for centuries, and today they still spark that dreamy 'what if I win?' excitement shared by hopefuls everywhere.

Established by the UN in 2023, World Lake Day highlights the vital role lakes play in providing fresh water, supporting wildlife and sustaining communities. It calls for cleaner shorelines and healthier waters through conservation, monitoring and restoration.

National Just Because Day is your free pass to do something for no reason at all. Send a surprise note, take a spontaneous day off, or do a small kindness — no occasion required, just because you can.

Festa do Vinho is Madeira's spirited wine harvest festival, filling the Portuguese island with tastings, grape-stomping, folk music and parades. Rooted in more than 500 years of winemaking, it invites visitors to experience the flavours and traditions of the vintage season.

Rtveli is Georgia's ancient grape harvest festival, a tradition stretching back over 8,000 years. Families gather to pick grapes, press them and ferment wine in clay qvevri vessels, celebrating with feasts, folk songs and toasts that honour the country's deep winemaking roots.

National Red Wine Day toasts the rich, storied world of red wine, from bold Cabernets to smooth Merlots. With winemaking roots stretching back thousands of years, it's the perfect day to swirl, sip and savour a glass — or discover a new favourite varietal.

Rainbow Bridge Remembrance Day is a gentle day to honour beloved pets who have passed away. Inspired by the tender poem of the Rainbow Bridge, it invites us to share memories, light a candle, and hold close the unconditional love our companions gave.

names.en: International Read Comics in Public Day

descriptions.en: Founded in 2010, International Read Comics in Public Day encourages fans to enjoy their favourite comics out in the open. By flipping pages on park benches and buses, readers celebrate the artistry of the medium and prove that comics are for everyone.

Raksha Bandhan is a cherished Hindu festival celebrating the bond between siblings. Sisters tie a decorative thread called a rakhi around their brother's wrist as a symbol of love and protection, and in return brothers promise to look after them — a heartfelt renewal of family ties.

slogans.en: A thread of love and protection.

descriptions.en: International Cosplay Day celebrates fans who bring beloved characters to life through costume and craft. From anime heroes to video-game villains, cosplayers gather for parades, photo shoots and contests that showcase creativity, skill and a global community of imagination.

Franchise Appreciation Day recognises the franchises that power local economies and create jobs in communities everywhere. From coffee shops to fitness studios, it's a day to thank the owners and teams behind familiar brands and support the small businesses that run them.

Individual Rights Day honours the birthday of philosopher John Locke, whose ideas shaped modern notions of liberty. It celebrates the fundamental rights every person deserves — life, liberty, property, free speech and freedom of belief — and the freedoms we too often take for granted.

India's National Sports Day honours the birthday of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand, winner of three Olympic golds. It celebrates the joy of playing and the power of sport to build health, discipline and pride — reminding everyone that showing up and giving your all is what counts.

Ginger Cat Appreciation Day celebrates the unique charm of orange-furred cats — their playful, affectionate personalities and the joy they bring as companions. From their five coat patterns (classic, mackerel, spotted, patched, ticked) to their famously skewed male-to-female ratio of roughly 3:1, ginger cats hold a special place in our homes and hearts, alongside famous fictional felines like Garfield and Puss in Boots.

slogans.en: Every ginger cat is a little tiger with a big heart.

descriptions.en: World Letter Writing Day celebrates the timeless art of hand-written correspondence. From scented paper to sealing wax, letters carry a personal touch that digital messages can never match. Founded by Richard Simpkin to revive the joy of finding a handwritten letter in the mailbox, the day encourages people to slow down and reconnect with friends, family, mentors, or even their future selves.

slogans.en: Put pen to paper. Send joy.

descriptions.en: National Hotel Employee Day, established in 2022 by the American Hotel & Lodging Association (AHLA), honors the nearly two million people working in the U.S. hotel industry. From early-morning front desks to late-night room service, these employees greet tired travelers, tidy rooms with care, and shape every guest's stay — making vacations, business trips, and weekend getaways possible.

slogans.en: Behind every great stay is a great team.

descriptions.en: Yogurt Day celebrates the creamy, nutrient-rich treat loved worldwide, observed September 1–3 each year. With roots in the Middle East and Central Asia thousands of years ago, modern yogurt comes in many forms — thick Greek, light non-fat, dairy-free — and delivers calcium, probiotics, and protein that support bones, gut health, and immunity.

slogans.en: Spoon into something good for you.

descriptions.en: Pierce Your Ears Day celebrates the tradition of ear piercing as a form of self-expression and cultural heritage. From ancient Egypt, where piercings signaled social standing, to sailors' protective talismans and today's bold ear stacks, the practice has marked milestones, reflected identity, and evolved into a celebrated art form.

National Live Fearless Day, founded in 2020 by Landry Champlin, encourages people to push past fear and act with courage. Whether tackling a personal fear, trying something new, or sharing a story of bravery, the day reminds us that courage means moving forward despite fear — and that the smallest brave step can spark a chain reaction of confidence.

slogans.en: Courage isn't the absence of fear. It's moving anyway.

descriptions.en: Read A New Book Month, observed throughout September, invites readers of all ages to dive into a new title. Trade books with friends, join a book club, donate old books, and get lost in whole new worlds between the pages — because a reader lives a thousand lives before they die.

slogans.en: Open a book. Open a world.

descriptions.en: Valentino Day commemorates the life and legacy of Rudolph Valentino, the Italian-born silent film star known as 'The Latin Lover,' who died on August 23, 1926. An estimated 100,000 people attended his funeral in New York City, and his death at just 31 shocked the world. The day pays homage to his short but iconic career in films like The Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse, The Sheik, and Son of the Sheik.

Find Your Inner Nerd Day is about dropping the mask and letting your quirks lead the way — whether you love space facts, board games, comic books, or coding projects. Founded in 2022 by speaker and author Beth Ziesenis, the day gives people a chance to share their true interests, especially the ones they might usually keep quiet. In 2026 it was officially added to the National Day Calendar.

slogans.en: Wear your weird like a badge.

descriptions.en: Merchant Navy Day, observed on September 3rd, honours the brave seafarers of the merchant fleet who keep global trade moving and remembers those lost at sea, especially during the World Wars. The date commemorates the SS Athenia, the first British merchant ship torpedoed by a German U-boat on 3 September 1939, the very day the Second World War began at sea.

slogans.en: The silent force that keeps the world turning.

descriptions.en: National Skyscraper Day is celebrated on September 3rd each year to mark the birthday of Louis H. Sullivan, the American architect widely regarded as the father of skyscrapers. From the world's first skyscraper — the ten-story Home Insurance Building in Chicago, 1885 — to today's 163-floor Burj Khalifa, the day honours the architects, engineers, and construction crews who keep pushing buildings toward the sky.

slogans.en: From ten stories to the sky.

descriptions.en: National Wildlife Day, observed on September 4th, raises awareness about endangered species and the urgent need to protect them. Founded in 2005 by animal behaviourist Colleen Paige, the day was later extended to February 22nd in memory of Steve Irwin following his death in 2006, making wildlife conservation a twice-yearly cause worth rallying around.

slogans.en: Protect the wild that protects us.

descriptions.en: International Taekwondo Day, celebrated on September 4th, marks the anniversary of the 1994 International Olympic Committee vote that brought taekwondo into the Olympic Games. Established in 2006 by World Taekwondo, the day honours the journey of a Korean martial art from post-war unification efforts to a global discipline practiced by millions on every continent.

World Beard Day, celebrated on the first Saturday of September, honours the beard and the cultures that have revered facial hair throughout history. From Viking beard traditions said to date back as far as 800 AD to modern competitions like the All Bearded Human Period world record set in Florida, the day celebrates every style from close-trimmed to full and bushy.

International Vulture Awareness Day, observed on the first Saturday of September, celebrates vultures and educates the public about their critical ecological role. Started in 2009 by South Africa's Birds of Prey Programme and the UK's Hawk Conservancy Trust, the day addresses misconceptions, supports vulture conservation, and reminds the world that these scavengers keep ecosystems healthy by removing carcasses before disease can spread.

Unification Day in Bulgaria, observed on September 6th, marks the 1885 unification of the Principality of Bulgaria with the autonomous region of Eastern Rumelia. The peaceful declaration in Plovdiv, led by revolutionary Zahari Stoyanov, united Bulgarian-speaking lands despite opposition from the Great Powers and helped define the modern Bulgarian state.

names.en: International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies
