descriptions.en: The International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies, observed on September 7th, raises awareness about air pollution as a public health and climate emergency. Established by the UN General Assembly in 2019 and first observed in 2020 under the coordination of UNEP, the day calls on individuals, communities, and governments to take collective action for cleaner air.

Labor Day, observed on the first Monday of September in the United States, honours the American worker and the labour movement that won safer conditions, fairer hours, and the weekend itself. Born from a New York City parade on September 5, 1882, it became a federal holiday in 1894 and now also marks the symbolic end of summer.

slogans.en: Honour the hands that built the country.

descriptions.en: The West Indian Day Parade fills Brooklyn's Eastern Parkway every Labor Day with Caribbean music, dance, and elaborate feathered costumes, drawing around two million spectators and participants. Founded by Trinidadian immigrant Jesse Waddle in the 1920s and moved to its current Labor Day slot in the 1960s, it is one of the largest cultural celebrations in North America.

slogans.en: One Caribbean, one Brooklyn, one parade.

descriptions.en: World Physical Therapy Day, observed on September 8th, honours the physical therapists who help people recover from injury, surgery, and chronic conditions through movement and exercise. Established in 1996 by World Physiotherapy on the anniversary of its own 1951 founding, the day celebrates the global community of clinicians who keep humanity moving.

International Pardon Day, observed on September 8th, marks the 1974 presidential proclamation by Gerald Ford that pardoned Richard Nixon for any crimes he may have committed during the Watergate scandal. The day invites people to set aside personal grudges and explore forgiveness as a deliberate act of strength rather than weakness.

Technical Analysts Day, observed on September 9th, celebrates the financial professionals who read charts, volume, and price patterns to navigate the markets. The date was chosen for its number — nine holds a special place in many technical theories — and the day honours a tradition stretching from Charles Dow's theories in the late 1800s to today's RSI, MACD, and Bollinger Band tools.

Teddy Bear Day on September 9 celebrates the stuffed companion named after Theodore Roosevelt, who in 1902 refused to shoot a captured bear. The toy that followed has comforted children — and plenty of adults — ever since.

World Dolphin Day, observed on September 12th, was established in 2022 by Sea Shepherd Global to commemorate the deadliest recorded cetacean slaughter in modern history — the September 12, 2021 killing of more than 1,400 white-sided dolphins off the Faroe Islands. The day raises awareness about the ongoing "grind" hunt and supports conservation of one of the ocean's most intelligent species.

slogans.en: Protect the minds of the sea.

descriptions.en: Gym Day, observed on September 12th, celebrates the motivation and community that comes from working out at a local gym. Founded in 2022 by fitness enthusiasts from the MyFitness sports club in Estonia and Latvia, the day kicks off autumn by encouraging people to build new fitness habits before the colder weather arrives.

German Language Day, observed on September 12th, celebrates the language spoken across Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, and parts of Italy and Belgium. Established by the German Language Association and endorsed by the United Nations, the day invites people to learn a few German words, try a translated classic, or simply appreciate a language that shares roughly 60% of its vocabulary with English.

National Police Woman Day, observed on September 12th in the United States, honours the women of American law enforcement. From Marie Owens, Chicago's first sworn female officer in 1891, to Alice Wells, who pioneered the Los Angeles Police Department's first female unit in 1910, the day celebrates a century-long fight for representation behind the badge.

slogans.en: Honour the women who answer the call.

descriptions.en: National Chocolate Milkshake Day, observed on September 12th in the United States, celebrates the drink made famous when a Walgreens employee in Chicago blended ice cream into a chocolate malt in 1922. The day invites everyone to enjoy the indulgent combination of ice cream, milk, and chocolate syrup — a simple pleasure that helped define American diner culture.

slogans.en: If it won't suck through a straw, it's not a milkshake.
